# PEUGEOT BOXER WORKSHOP MANUAL 2006 - 2017

You will see that this workshop manual is for the Citron Jumper. Don't worry, the Peugeot Boxer was badged the Citroën Jumper in a lot of countries and is also known as the Citroen Relay, Fiat Ducato, Peugeot Manager and the Ram Promaster. Your workshop manual deals with the 3rd generation Peugeot Boxer which was launched in 2006. All the models (Jumper, Ducato, Relay, Boxer, Manager etc) allshare the same design and engineering, with only subtle trim changes between each brand. So don't worry, you have the correct manual.

# 1. Foreword

# 1.1. Units of pressure

1/ Units of pressure in bars.

N.B. : One bar has the advantage of being close to the average atmospheric pressure at sea level.

2/ Unit of pressure in millimetres of mercury (symbol: mmHg) or Torr (symbol: Torr).   
This unit of measurement of pressure was origially defined as the pressure exerted at 0°C by a 1 milimetre column of mercury, later indexed to the atmospheric pressure.   
The pressure values indicated in the tables below are the values read on the pressure gauge (Relative pressure).

N.B. : Relative pressure is equal to absolute pressure minus atmospheric pressure.

# 1.2. Units of tension

The SEEM unit measures by deflection of the static tension of the belt, by deforming a portion of its length.

# 8. Pressure, engine end of compression

Measure the pressure at the end of compression, in order, on cylinders 1, 2,3 and 4.

N.B. : The difference in pressure between 2 cylinders must not exceed 5 bars.

CAUTION : Always search for the origins of fault(s), where the values measured are found to be significantly out.

# 2. Removing

# 2.1. Common operations

CAUTION : Replace the torsional vibration damper double pulley for a distance travelled greater than or equal t 160000 km, when the accessories drive belt is replaced.

Place the vehicle on a 2-post lift.   
Disconnect the battery negative terminal.

Remove :

The protection plates under the engine The front right wheel

CAUTION : Prior to removal, and before any subsequent refittig of the ancillary drive belt that has been removed, it is compulsory for the engine to be at ambient temperature (Below 0 C). In alother cases, replace the ancillay drive belt.

N.B. : Removing it with the engine hot causes irreversible and invisible damage to the ancillary drive belt.

CAUTION : If replacing it, cut and remove the ancillary drive belt.

CAUTION : Check that the tool [0198-P] is correctly positioned between two teeth of the flywheel; or turn the crankshaft to correctly position the tool.

Move aside and secure : The starter motor  .

Slacken the fixing bolt (2) of the ancillary drive pulley by 2 cm.

# 4. Verification

Remove one accessories drive pulley fixing bolt .   
Set the gearbox in neutral. Fit the tool [0198-M1].   
Secure the tool [0198-M1] ; Using the screws [0198-M2].   
Fit the tool [0198-M3].   
Tighten the bolt [0198-M4] .   
Rotate the crankshaft clockwise ; Check that the accessories drive pulley is not warped.   
Engage 1st gear.   
Remove the tools [0198].

1. Cleaning The use of a "high pressure" cleaner is prohibited.

2. Fuel supply system Recommended fuel : Diesel.

3. Electrical circuit

Switching an injection ECU from one vehicle to another will make it impossible to start either vehicle.   
Do not supply a diesel injector with 12 volts.

4. high pressure fuel pump

![](images/b442f27b43e1490a701e0a5e0ea0d2593f5621b0519332089c53f6ee171b3db8.webp)

The high pressure outlet union "b" (malfunction) Fuel inlet "a" •Fuel return "c"

# 5. Diesel injector

CAUTION : Cleaning operations using diesel and ultrasound are prohibited.

![](images/b930be76b1b2f296a67dc77a29824f8348690a9ec2dc8412cecfd54b74ee7ef9.webp)  
Figure : B1BK3YED

Do not separate the diesel injector body (2) from the following components : Diesel injector "f" (replacement parts not available) Electromagnetic element "d" (replacement parts not available)

Do not turn the nut "e" (malfunction).   
Calamine cleaning on the injector nose is prohibited.

6. Fuel high pressure common injection rails

![](images/440489cd19b079a674aa5e4322fb74964afac77b5f9d67c6eed618e53a4d4c22.webp)  
Figure : B1BK3YFD

Do not separate the fuel high pressure sensor "g" from the common injection rail (replacement parts not available)

# 1. Protection

CAUTION : Always plug the apertures straightaway after opening up the fuel circuit; Using the specific plugs kit

# 2. Cleaning

CAUTION : The use of a "high pressure" cleaner is prohibited.

CAUTION : Do not use compressed air.

# 3. Fuel supply system

Recommended fuel : Diesel.

CAUTION : Do not use fuel other than diesel (Risk of destruction of the injection system and of the engine).

CAUTION : The addition of additives such as fuel circuit cleaner/remetalliser, is prohibited.

# 4. Electrical circuit

Exchanging an engine management ECU between two vehicles makes it impossible to start the vehicles.

CAUTION : Do not supply a diesel injector with 12 volts.

5. high pressure fuel pump

![](images/c88be39a2aaa168dc004adc0715790e603da8657861f90f283df973909d614ed.webp)  
Figure : B1BK3YND

Do not separate the ring seal from the high pressure fuel pump (1) (at "b") (No replacement parts).

CAUTION : Cleaning operations using diesel and ultrasound are prohibited.

![](images/d8168653faac5e70f8dd794e2c5c07f438bd7c34854cb798704bdcefde22e352.webp)

JUMPER IlB1Gl0138P0 - Drain and refill - Reilling - Bleeding : Cooling system

Close the bleed screw when the fluid is flowing freely without any air bubbles.

3.2. Filling using the tool for filling the cooling system by vacuum

CAUTION : Always use new coolant.

Connect the hose (1) (at "a") ; Using tool [0165-2].

# N.B. : Refit new clips .

Close the bleed screw .   
Put the equipment for filling by vacuum [01102] in place on the expansion bottle .

CAUTION : To avoid entry of air into the circuit, provide for 20 % additional coolant.

Prepare a receptacle of coolant containing the quantity of fluid drained + 20 %.

N.B. : The receptacle must be positioned slightly lower than the equipment for filing by vacuum.

![](images/b80b6bbaec4cdcbf629abba5eaec1bdd041d8a79b1340dfacb3ca69a8a6e3c5c.webp)  
Figure : B1GI09CD

Wait 10 seconds and check that the value obtained does not drop Fillthe cooling circuit completely and wait for the return to 0 bar (diagram "D")

N.B. : The quantity of coolant filled should correspond to the quantity of fluid drained.

Repeat the operation until the cooling system is full(if necessary).

JUMPER Il - B1Gl0138P0 - Drain and refill - Reilling - Bleeding : Cooling system

CAUTION : Remove the equipment for filing by vacuum [01102] and rinse the assembly with clean water.

4. Degassing and checking the cooling system

Open the rod on the filling cylinder .   
Start the engine.

N.B. : The air conditioning control should not operate during this phase.

4.1. Toutes motorisations sauf norme de dépollution EURO 6 Keep the engine speed at 15002000 rpm, up to the second cooling cycle (cooling fan(s) cuting in and out).

CAUTION : Check that there are no coolant leaks.

# 4.2. Diesel engine Euro 6

The cutting in of the fan assembly for 10 seconds indicates the switch to after sales degas mode.   
Accelerate to an engine speed above 2300 rpm for more than 10 seconds to switch to degas mode.   
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 rpm until the fan assembly cuts in again.

4.3. Degassing and checking the cooling system (continued)

CAUTION : Check that the level of coolant in the filling cylinder is sufficient.

Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Do not remove the filling cylinder while the engine is hot.

Leave the engine to cool.   
Blank the filling cylinder using the blocking rod .   
Remove the filling cylinder , plug and adapter assembly.   
Check the coolant level when cold.   
Top up the coolant to the "max" level (Cold).

CAUTION : Do not fill the system past the max mark.

Refit and tighten the cap on the header tank .

CAUTION : Check that the cooling system fillr cap is locked (For bayonet cap).

# CHECK : FUEL HIGH PRESSURE SUPPLY CIRCUIT

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations  .

CAUTION : Before carrying out any work on the high pressure fuel supply circuit, read the faults memory anc carry out the actuator tests available in the diagnostic tool .

# 1. Tooling

![](images/8d755fa1c74e80ca5408eea8f19041e891ec0ca56f21323d6453b7b31f861a70.webp)

JUMPER IIB1HD0151PO - Check : Fuel high pressure supply circuit

![](images/935e96121a46b5af6c7575905c91ea37ec5e1223e70ce0d814b8003821f734d4.webp)

# 2. Removing

Remove the engine style cover .

3. Preliminary checks

3.1. Low pressure fuel circuit

Check the following components :

The quantity of fuel in the tank : 15 litres minimum   
Fuel qualityif in doubt over the fuel quality, use an auxiliary tank with a filter, filled with fuel which you know where it came from)   
•That there are no leaks on the high pressure fuel circuit   
The low pressure fuel supply circuit (ilter clogged, condition of the pipes, no air bubbles) : Refer to the low pressure fuel circuit checking method

# 3.2. Electrical circuit

Remove the engine style cover . Check the elements which could cause system malfunctions :

The battery charge The deactivation of the engine immobiliser •The condition of the connectors and electrical harnesses

JUMPER IIB1HD0151PO - Check : Fuel high pressure supply circuit

The classfication of the injectors ; Using the diagnostic equipment

4. Checking the fuel high pressure circuit

4.1. Check : Fuel pressure regulation

![](images/a1b73ef18457e3dcd089908ba5be494d0733f99fc73d72b9d7773a85510f52c1.webp)  
Figure : B1HDZL2D

Disconnect injectors (at "a").

Connect the diagnostic tool to the vehicle's diagnostic socket ; Select in succession the following menus :

, Parameter Measurements menu • Fuel circuit information • Fuel pressure ordered - Measured fuel pressure

Operate the starter for 5 seconds ; Read the maximum values of the ordered and measured pressures on the diagnosti tool simultaneously.

CAUTION : The ordered and measured pressures must be identical (± 40 bars) and 120 bars minimum.

N.B. : If the pressures read are identical, the system is providing suficient pressure to start and operate normally Confirm the preliminary checks, otherwise contact the technical assistance platform.

N.B. :If the pressures read are different, the system does not have the pressure required : Check the leak return fron the pump and from the injectors.

Connect the connectors (at "a").

4.2. Check the high pressure pump

![](images/b60be157b4950025f4400e5bec40a0aec02c3cdd3dcfc64165289c9be2b5be58.webp)  
Figure : B1HDZL3D

Disconnect the fuel pressure regulator (at "c").   
Uncouple connection (at "b").   
Couple the tool [1613-G] on the high pressure fuel pump (at "b").

CAUTION : Close the union ; Using tool [1617-J].

Abide by the following conditions :

Fuel pressure regulator disconnected (at "c") Unions on the low pressure fuel return pipe plugged

Operate the starter motor for 15 seconds.

CAUTION : The maximum volume collected should not exceed 25 ml.

N.B. : In the case of a volume which exceeds this value, replace the high pressure pump then repeat the check.

CAUTION : Carefully clean, plug and store the tool used.

Remove the tool [1613-G].   
Disconnect the fuel pressure regulator (at "c").   
Connect the union (at "b").

4.3. Injector check

![](images/c67d03488b9a90c00d1d2f1fedfba9874e0bed29d541b06cfea012911084efdd.webp)

CAUTION : The fuel recovered is not compatible with engine versions that do not have particle filters.

The fuel which is retrieved contains an additive for particulate emission filter requirements. The quantity of additive injected into the fuel tank corresponds to the quantity of fuel and is defined by the fuel additive adding ECU.

Put back all of the fuel recovered.

If the fuel taken during the draining operation is not re-usable (water or impurities present), proceed as follows :

Place the cap on the fuel tank   
• Switch on the ignition for 5 seconds (minimum) Switch off the ignition   
• Remove the plug Refill the tank

N.B. : This operation enables the fuel additive adding ECU to inject the quantity of additive corresponding to the quantity of diesel added.

# FORCED REGENERATION : PARTICLE FILTER (TECHNICAL NOTE)

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

ESSENTIAL : Wait at least one hour before carrying out any work on the exhaust line.

# 1. Tooling

Diagnostic tool.

# 2. Forced regeneration of the particle emission filter

ESSENTIAL : Respect the safety and cleanliness recommendations that are specificto high pressure diesel injection (HDi) engines.

ESSENTIAL : Where the recommended installation is not available, carry out the forced regeneration of the particle filtr outside the workshop, on an area of hard standing and remote from any inflammable materials. Make the work area secure. Ensure that no one passes or stands behind the vehicle during the forced regeneration. Put the vehicle in the "high" position (vehicle with hydraulic suspension). Check that there are no aerosols or inflammable products inside the boot. Wear heat-resistant gloves. Connect the vehicle to an approved gas extractor for this type of operation.

CAUTION : Check that the level of fuel in the tank is sufficient (minimum 20 litres).

CAUTION : Check the following fluid levels : Engine oil ; Coolant.

CAUTION : Check : The tightness of the turbocharging hoses (Risk of uncoupling).

ESSENTIAL : Remove the under-engine protection.

Start the engine and allow it to warm up (65°C minimum).   
Connect the diagnostic tool on the vehicle's central socket.

Carry out :

Fault reading (Engine ECU) Fault clearing

Trigger the particle emission filter forced regeneration cycle ; Using the diagnostic equipment.   
After the regeneration cycle : Alow the engine to run at idle, with the bonnet open, to help the cooling.   
Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Wait at least one hour before carrying out any work on the exhaust line. Wear heat-resistant gloves.

Refit the under-engine protection .

New vehicles delivered to customers now have a hydrometer which permits direct displaying of the charge status.

# 1. Application

This procedure applies to all ready-to-use batteries.   
They are fitted on new vehicles or sold as Replacement Parts (boutique, warehouse, gondola end.….).   
The batteries must guarantee quality and reliability which meet the requirements of our customers.   
They are an addition to the new vehicle preparation ranges distributed for each model of the range.

# 2. Recommended tools

Approved charging equipment : See garage equipment catalogue or, failing this, obtain a limited voltage charger Approved battery cable.

# 3. General principles for charging batteries

:omply with the maximum voltage indications and the nominal current level in relation to the type and size of the batter

Never apply an excessive voltage or current   
Use a charger suited to the battery and the type of charge required   
Do not use a rapid charger or, if the charger has this function, use the normal charge function   
Check the condition of the battery

N.B. : The effectiveness of the charge depends on the condition of the battery.

# 4. Precautions to be taken

Do not charge :

A faulty battery (White hydrometer)   
A battery coated with sulphate (Depositing of a superficial layer of lead sulphate on the plates)   
A warm battery (Risk of thermal racing and damage)

5. Charging procedure

5.1. Preliminary operations

![](images/8df7c30c3b55b3cfd878e9c8be564d254c4be63a452b3b308a16fd0f033566fe.webp)  
Figure : D1CP03JD

Remove the battery (1) located underneath the passenger compartment floor.

CAUTION : If the hydrometer is white, the battery is faulty : Replace the battery.

Check the conformity of the battery :

Sealing of the case   
Absence of electrolyte leaks Absence of apparent signs of impact or cracks   
, Status of the hydrometer

N.B. : Date of manufacture (If the battery was manufactured more than 6 months ago : Replace the battery).

# 5.2. Charging

Follow the operating instructions given by the manufacturer of the charger .

Check the clamps and terminals are clean .If the terminals are covered with sulphate (whitish or greenish deposit), str and clean them.

The recharging operation must be carried out in a ventilated environment away from naked flames or any sources of sparks to prevent any risk of explosion and fire.

Do not recharge a frozen battry;i must first be thawed out to prevent the risk of an explosion;if it has frozen, have the battery checked before recharging by a specialist; they willcheck that the internal components have not been damagec and that the casing is not cracked, which would mean that toxic and corrosive acid could leak.

case of batteries with topping of up of the electrolyte only :

Connect the battery to the charger starting with the positive cable Check the level  15 mm above the plates) and top up with distilled water (if necessary)

CAUTION : In the case of batteries which do not require maintenance, removal of the caps and topping up with fluid is strictly prohibited.

# 5.3. Automatic charger

Use the normal charging programme (Rapid charging prohibited).

5.4. Charger with limited voltage

Adjust the charging current to 1/20 of the capacity(example: 45Ah provides a charging current of 2,25A) for a charging time of 6 to 12 hours.

# 5.5. Limited voltage charger

Charge with a voltage limited to 14,8 V for 12 hours with a current limited to 1/4 of the capacity.

5.6. Precautions to be taken (Battery charge)

Monitor the progressof the charge regularly, ensuring in particular that the battery does not get excessively warm or does not start to bubble. When the charge is complete, first switch off the charger and then disconnect the battery.

# 6. Check following charging

Check the colour of the hydrometer :

If it is green : The battery is correct   
Refit the battery on the vehicle   
fit is not green: An additional charge is necessary, until the hydrometer turns green, without exceeding the time defined   
After 2 unsuccessful charging cycles, the battery is faulty   
Replace the battery

# 1. Standards in force

The classification of the engine oils is established by the following recognised bodies :

S.A.E. : Society of Automotive Engineers   
API : American Petroleum Institute   
ACEA : Association des Constructeurs Europeens d'Automobiles

# 2. S.A.E. standards

2.1. Engine oil grade selection table The choice of engine oil grade depends on the climate of the country.

2.2. Préconisation des grades de viscosités

Choice of the various grades of viscosity remains dependent on use of the vehicle in the types of limate defined in the diagram below . Par exemple, 'utilisation du grade 10W 40 se limite aux pays tempérés (de -17  +37 C) ou à clim chaud.

N.B. : For any other application, the grade has to be chosen as a function of the climatic zone of the country where the vehicle is to be used.

# 3. ACEA standards

3.1. Petrol and diesel mixed oils recommended by PSA

The meaning of the first letter does not change, it always refers to the engine type :

A = Petrol and petrol/LPG dual fuel engines B = diesel engines

The next figure does change and refers to the following types of oil :

3 = High performance oils   
4 = Oils specific to certain direct injection diesel engines   
5 = Oils with very high performance, favouring lower fuel consumption

Examples :

ACEA A3/B3 : Huiles mixtes hautes performances et bicarburation essence/GPL ACEA A5/B5 : Blended oils with very high performance, for all engines, favouring fuel economy

CAUTION : Since 2004, the ACEA has imposed mixed oils : A1/B1 , A3/B3, A3/B4, A5/B5. Therefore, al lubricant recommended by PSA are mixed ; There are no longer any oils specific to petrol or diesel.

3.2. Introduction of low ash content oils (LOw SAPS)

Oils with low ash content reduce the amount of particles entering the exhaust and so help lengthen the life ofthe partick filter. The ash content changes from 1,3 % in current oils to 0,8 % in these new oils (maximum permitted values).

N.B. : LOW SAPS (Sulphated Ash Phosphorus Sulphur).

New specifications ACEA :

C3 : Moderate ash content • C2 : Moderate ash content and fuel economy • C1 : Very low ash content and fuel economy

The C2 oil, specific to PSA, corresponds to a request to reduce the ash within a reasonable cost limit while maintaining fuel economy requirements. The C2 oil i a petrol and diesel mixed oil with energy economy particularly suited to engines fited with a particle filter.

# 4. API oil standards

The meaning of the first lettr does not change, it always refers to the engine type :

S = Petrol and petrol/LPG dual fuel engines •C = diesel engines

The second letter corresponds to the evolution level of the oil (in rising order).   
Example : The standard SL is stricter than the standard SJ and corresponds to an improved level of performance.

# 5. Qualité des huiles moteur

The engine lubrication oils are classified in line with 3 quality levels :

Mineral oil or level 1 PSA Semi-synthetic oil or level 2 PSA Synthetic oil or level 3 PSA

IUMPER IlE4ABoMPO - Maintenance : Recommended ingredients, year 2006

ESSENTIAL : To ensure that the engines retain their performance, it is essential that only high quality engine oil is used : Level 2 PSA minimum (synthetic or semi-synthetic oils).

CAUTION : L'huile minérale ne peut ètre utilisée que sur les véhicules équipés de la motorisation type 384F.

CAUTION : For vehicles sold from model year 1999 (7/98), in accordance with the normal maintenance plan, the use of an approved semi-synthetic oil is imperative.

# 6. Nouvelle huile à économie de carburant et antipollution

Cete huile contribue aux objectis d'économie d'énergie et de réductions des émissions poluantes visés par le groupe concerne plus particulièrement les véhicules diesel équipés de filtres à particules.

N.B. : Se référer au Chapitre 8 : restrictions pour toutes applications avec cette huile.

CAUTION : L'huile à уГПОПНЙЕ Д'уОЕТЗЙЕ 5W30, au périmètre d'application restreint, notamment sur moteurs HD avec filtre à particules et moteurs à essence XU10J4RS, EW10J4S, EW12J4, EW12E4, EW10A, EW7A est retirée progressivement de la commercialisation.

# 7. Recommendations(in normal driving conditions)

Les moteurs PSA sont lubrifiés en premire monte avec de I'huile TOTAL ACTIVA/QUARTZ INEO ECS, aux proprités уГПОПНЙЕ de carburant et Antipollution.

Respecter les intervalles de vidanges standards :

For vehicles with maintenance interval of 30 000 km (20 000 miles), use exclusively one of the oils TOTAL ACTIVA / QUARTZ 7000, 9000 or INEO ECS or any other oils with equivalent specifications. The specifications these oils are higher than those defined by standard ACEA A3/B3 or API SL/CF . Failing this, you should follow the maintenance schedules for severe operating conditions In the case of Diesel vehicles with Particle Filter, for lasting optimum operation of the PEFs, the use of low ash content oil TOTAL ACTIVA INEO ECS for France and TOTAL QUARTZ INEO ECS outside France is particularly recommended (Or any other oils with equivalent specifications)

AUTION : During the bleeding operation : Keep the fluid topped up in the reservoir and complete it.

.B. : Use only clean fluid free from bubbles. Avoid any introduction of impurities into the hydraulic systen

1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit

CAUTION : Do not switch on the ignition at any time during the operation.

N.B. : Bleed the primary circuit until clean, non-foaming brake fluid is obtained.

There are 2 procedures for bleeding the primary brake circuit.

1.1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit (With the bleeding device) Bleed the circuit following the instructions for use of the equipment. 1.2. Bleeding the primary braking circuit (without brake bleeding equipment)

# N.B. : Two operators are necessary.

Couple a transparent tube on the bleed screw .   
Press the brake pedal slowly.   
Open the bleed screw .   
Hold the pedal fully down.   
Close the bleed screw .   
Allow the brake pedal to return naturally.   
Repeat the operation until the fluid running out is clean and free from air bubbles.   
Proceed in the same way for the other wheels.

N.B. : Check that the wheels rotate freely when the parking brake is released .

1.3. Checking : Bleeding the primary braking circuit

At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the travel of the brake pedal (no extension).   
If the travel is long and spongy, repeat the bleed procedure.   
Start the engine.   
Check the travel of the brake pedal (no extension) ; Road test the vehicle (if necessary).   
If brake pedal travel is not correct ; Bleed the secondary brake circuit.

# 2. Bleed the secondary brake circuit

Bleeding of the secondary braking circuit is done with a diagnostic tool.   
This procedure is only carried out if the primary brake circuit has been bled.   
Continue the procedure for bleeding of the hydraulic circuit as defined by the diagnostic tool.   
At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the brake pedal travel (no extension), otherwise repeat the bleeding procedure.

# 1. Main braking circuit

# 1.1. all versions

Diagonally split braking circuit with ABS and EBA. Disc brakes at the front and at the rear :

The front brake discs are ventilated The rear brake discs are non-ventilated

The principal brake compensator and limiter functions are provided by the ABS brake force distribution system.

ABS : Anti-lock brakes REF : Electronic braking distribution AFU (EBA) : Emergency Braking Assistance

The front brake pads are fitted with a wear indicator on the inner left pad .

1.2. Depending on the versions

Braking system with ABS and ASR.   
Braking system with ESP, ASR and hill start assistance.

Key:

ESP : Dynamic stability control Traction control : Traction control

Hil srt assanetiAsss herivemiofn foard geaeewhnheii ndnt omo tha2%. The hil start asstance is activated automatially when the brake pedal is pressed and the following conditions are met :

The vehicle is stationary о The gradient is more than 2 % э The clutch pedal is pressed

# 1. Recommended tools

![](images/03ab5e6e53e71cab67799c10e50ef3763642f665ddd0a9a46fa40fc8048d84ab.webp)

Figure : E5AP2XHD [2] dial gauge 2437-T.

# 2. Preliminary operation

Untighten the rear wheel bolts.   
Raise and support the vehicle, with the rear wheels hanging free.   
Remove the rear wheels.

![](images/bfa017e19d60f1f0c7be19cf8eebd1ffce20a6dcf8afe2233ba6e345f300d405.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KND

Remove :

The rear brake pads (see the relevant operation) The bolts (1)

Move aside and suspend the brake caliper (2).

# 3. Checking the thickness

![](images/fb7d43dbcf1ea1d00cd40ff38202de619f8416a9104d998ec43592b54ef84e1a.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KPD

Use a 0/50 mm micrometer.   
Max. thickness variation on one circumference = 0,025 mm .   
Nominal thickness : 15,9/16,2 mm .   
Min. permissible thickness (wear) : 14,2 mm .   
Always replace the discs that are not as thick as the value shown.   
In the case of damage or deep scratches, the surfaces of the disc may be ground.   
Minimum permitted thickness after grinding : 14,55 mm .

4. Checking the run-out

![](images/fca81cc1c9f1fe046f3c3665a1783bbf3c847b966c3c0e1e52a066366ce9a7dd.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KQD

Fix the magnetic support [1] on the spring leaf.   
Attach the dial gauge [2] to the magnetic bracket [1].   
The brake disc run-out check is carried out at approximately 2 mm from the outside diameter.   
Turn the brake disc by a full rotation.   
Maximum run-out = 0,030 mm .

5. Brake disc inside diameter check

![](images/dd8656c5bb612bfc122e82b9013ea0498889445927965052690a618d091f717d.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7K7D

Remove : The bolts (3) The rear brake disc

![](images/15495fe42f28e4db9f968146cf7184fe7885d969f7c6e350e138a78a2fbd53a5.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KRD

A : Disc brake bore diameter : Nominal diameter : 172/172,15 mm Maximum permitted diameter after wear : 173 mm

Brake shoe lining : Min. permissible thickness = 1,5 mm .

# 6. Additional operations

Refit : The rear brake disc The bolts (3)

Tighten the bolts (3) to 1,2 ± 0,1 daN.m.   
Position the brake caliper (2).   
Refit the bolts (1) (new) (pre-coated with a thread locking product).   
Tighten the bolts (1) to 16 ± 0,5 daN.m.   
Fit the brake pads (see the relevant operation).   
Apply the brakes, with the engine running, several times before driving the vehicle.   
Check the operation of the brakes.   
Refit the rear wheels.   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten the wheel bolts .

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

# 3. Cleaning

ESSENTIAL : Do not use compressed air to clean the brakes.

# 3.1. 1st possibility

Clean the brake disc and the brake caliper, using an approved brake cleaning product.   
Allow to dry and to drain.

Wipe with a paper towel.

3.2. 2nd possibility Use an approved dedusting instrument (refer to the Material and Equipment Catalogue).

4. Refitting

Refit :

The brake pads (2) о The retaining clips (3) The spring (4) ; Using tool [1] The spring (5) The adjusting mechanism (1)

Thoroughly clean the disc/hub bearings.

Refit :

The rear hub (see the relevant operation) The rear brake disc (see the relevant operation)

Adjust the parking brake (see the relevant operation).   
Apply the brakes, with the engine running, several times before driving the vehicle.   
Check the operation of the brakes.   
Refit the rear wheels.   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten the wheel bolts .

# 3. Bleeding the brake system

CAUTION : During the bleeding operation : Keep the fluid topped up in the reservoir and complete it. Use new brake fluid only.

Bleed the primary brake circuit during a conventional operation. Bleed the secondary brake circuit in the following cases :

Venting the secondary brake circuit Starting the pump supply to the electrovalves

3.1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit

CAUTION : The ABS system must not be in operation during the bleeding procedure

Use a bleed tool approved by the manufacturer.

• RH rear • Left hand front • Left hand rear Right hand front

Figure : B3FP7NBD

Perform the following operations :

Couple a transparent pipe (4) to the bleed screw   
• Submerge the other end of the tube into a clean receptacle   
• Open the bleed screw   
, Wait for the liquid to flow without air bubbles Close the bleed screw Remove the bleeding equipment .   
Check the brake fluid level (between the "MIN" level and the "MAX" level).   
If necessary, fill with approved and recommended synthetic brake fluid.

# 3.2. Bleed the secondary brake circuit (ABS/ESP hydraulic block)

N.B. : The equipment to be bled is always connected to the brake fluid reservoir

Select a diagnostic tool.   
Connect the diagnostic tool.   
From the screen of the diagnostic tool, select the menu : "ABS PURGE".   
Follow the instructions on the diagnostic tool.   
Bleed the brakes observing the order indicated (ABS type bleeding operation).   
At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the brake pedal travel (no extension), otherwise repeat the bleeding procedure.   
Remove the tools.

CAUTION : Always check the oil level using the dipstick.

Oil change interval : Refer to the maintenance schedule.

N.B. : Values given as an indication.

# 1. Flexible ancillary drive belt

ESSENTL

CAUTION : Mark the direction of rotation of the ancillary drive belt before removing it.

CAUTION : If re-using the existing accessories drive belt, refit it in the correct fitting direction.

CAUTION : Check that the rollers turn freely (no play and no tightness).

# 2. Visual check

Check that the timing belt is free of cracks and traces of oil.   
Check the absence of oil leaks (crankshaft and camshaft sealing rings).   
Check the absence of coolant fluid leaks (Coolant pump).   
Check that the track of the engine speed sensor target is not distorted or scratched.

N.B. : Replace any defective parts.

# Remove :

The central section of the lower front panel (see the relevant operation) The right-hand headlamp (see the relevant operation) The front wheels The protective panel under the engine The drive shafts (see the relevant operation) The pre-catalytic converter (see the relevant operation)

The cooling radiator pipes   
The turbocharger air cooler pipe ( right hand side)   
The heater matrix inlet and outlet hoses   
The expansion bottle pipe   
The fuel supply and return pipes

# 1. Protection

CAUTION : Always plug the apertures straightaway after opening up the fuel circuit ; Using the specific plugs kit.

# 2. Cleaning

CAUTION : The use of a "high pressure" cleaner is prohibited.

CAUTION : Do not use compressed air.

# 3. Fuel supply system

Recommended fuel : Diesel.

CAUTION : Do not use fuel other than diesel (Risk of destruction of the injection system and of the engine).

CAUTION : The addition of additives such as fuel circuit cleaner/remetallser, is prohibited.

# 4. Electrical circuit

Exchanging an engine management ECU between two vehicles makes it impossible to start the vehicles.

CAUTION : Do not supply a diesel injector with 12 volts.

# 5. high pressure fuel pump

![](images/0b9e27117156473df184769a58b2df503d42b545aafe018b1133100185f2d9eb.webp)  
Figure : B1BK3YND

Do not separate the ring seal from the high pressure fuel pump (1) (at "b") (No replacement parts).

# 6. Diesel injector

CAUTION : Cleaning operations using diesel and ultrasound are prohibited.

![](images/6a1fd8e2e522465ec5383c2c347d0a13fefd6b1de0bd306f21dc83d300f9d353.webp)  
Figure : B1BK3YQD

Do not separate the diesel injector body (2) from the following components :

•High pressure union (at "d") (malfunction) Diesel injector (at "e") (replacement parts not available) Electromagnetic element (at "c") (replacement parts not available)

Calamine cleaning on the injector nose is prohibited.

# 2. Removing

ESSENTIAL : Respect the safety and cleanlinessrecommendations that are specific t high pressure diesel ijection (HDi) engines.

Place the vehicle on a 2-post lift.   
Remove the under engine protection .   
Place a draining tray under the engine. Disconnect the connector (at "a").   
Remove the oil pressure switch (1).

![](images/838b9da76135a1464fb9a2f5057522b7391ea9997605db60e2058bc9e5191f8f.webp)

Figure : B1FD073D

![](images/27ee0160ed5eb8642941bc2eac0dae31c1a4590879559ad69ec812c008879222.webp)  
Figure : B1BD04PD

Fit the tool assembly [1503-AY] and [1503-B] to tool [1503-L].

Onu nov . Un pressure is cheureu win tne engne not after checking the oil level.

Start the engine.   
Wait for the fan to engage and then disengage.   
Note the oil pressure.   
Compare the readings on the oil pressure gauge with those in the table .   
Wait for the engine to cool down.   
Remove the tools [1503-AY], [1503-B], [1503-L].

# 4. Refitting

Clean the thread of the oil pressure switch (1).   
Coat the thread of the oil pressure switch (1) with thread lock.   
Refit the oil pressure switch (1) ; Tighten to 4 ± 0,4 daN.m.   
Reconnect the connector (at "a").   
Top up to level.   
Start the engine.   
Check the sealing of the oil pressure switch .   
Refit the under-engine protection .   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.

# 2. Draining the cooling system

CAUTION : The draining operation is carried out with the engine cold.

Put the vehicle on a hoist.

Remove :

The protective panel under the engine (according to equipment) The de-aeration chamber plug (Carefully)

N.B. : Place a clean tray underneath the engine to recover the coolant.

![](images/ebd7862ffa32150c8ef668f3019fa18f7abeae44f1e2d4bee3a81e23e753f97c.webp)  
Figure : B1GI00MD

Uncouple the pipe (1) (at "a") ; Using tool [0165-2].   
Open the bleed screws located on the coolant outlet housing and the heater pipe.   
Allow the coolant to run out.   
Drain the cylinder block (if necessary).

CAUTION : If the toolfo filing the cooling system by vacuum [01102] is used, measure the quantity of coolant drained.

# 3. Filling the cooling system

CAUTION : If the cooling system is contaminated, rinse with clean water

CAUTION : Always use new coolant.

;AUTION : Each filling operation must always be followed by a cooling system degas operatior http://127.0.0.1:6091/affiche.do?ref=B1GI0138P0&refaff=B1GI0138P0&typeDoc=2&idFct=FCT0512

3.1. Filing the cooling system by gravity Connect the hose (1) (at "a") ; Using tool [0165-2].

N.B. : Refit new clips .

![](images/731fdfb915b3dfd096bb15f5b074f07633ad0bb627ef3a3ad603600569a5c3aa.webp)  
Figure : B1GI09DD

"A" : Fitting with filling cylinder offset ; Using the tools [0173], [0173-B], [0173-C].   
"B" : Fitting with filing cylinder direct ; Using tool [0173-2].   
Fit the filling cylinder , blank and adaptor assembly on the expansion chamber (according to assembly).   
Open the rod on the filling cylinder .   
Slowly fill the cooling system with clean coolant.   
Close the bleed screw when the fluid is flowing freely without any air bubbles.

N.B. : The filling cylinder should be filled to the 1 litre mark for correct bleeding of the heater matrix.

3.2. Filling using the tool for filling the cooling system by vacuum

CAUTION : Always use new coolant.

Connect the hose (1) (at "a") ; Using tool [0165-2].

N.B. : Refit new clips .

Close the bleed screw .   
Put the equipment for filling by vacuum [01102] in place on the expansion bottle .

CAUTION : To avoid entry of air into the circuit, provide for 20 % additional coolant

Prepare a receptacle of coolant containina the auantitv of fluid drained + 20 %.

N.B. : Ihe receptacle must be positioned slightly lower than the equipment for filling by vacuum.

![](images/215c30a2a1268d56f6ba7713c9db03d1125c373cc2e61a68e02542db20e9dc0f.webp)  
Figure : B1GI09CD

Place the cooling circuit under a vacuum to reach -0,9 bar (diagram "C") : Wait 10 seconds and check that the value obtained does not drop Fil the cooling circuit completely and wait for the return to 0 bar (diagram "D")

http://127.0.0.1:6091/affiche.do?ref=B1Gl0138P0&refaff=B1GI0138P0&typeDoc=2&idFct=FCT0512

N.B. : The quantity of coolant filled should correspond to the quantity of fluid drained.

Repeat the operation until the cooling system is full(if necessary).

CAUTION : Remove the equipment for flling by vacuum [01102] and rinse the assembly with clean water.

# 4. Degassing and checking the cooling system

Fit theca ircoeantsmblnhete inhaofiuhol  ili c.   
Open the rod on the filing cylinder .   
Start the engine.

N.B. : The air conditioning control should not operate during this phase.

4.1. Toutes motorisations sauf norme de dépollution EURO 6

Keep the engine speed at 15002000 rpm, up to the second cooling cycle (cooling fan(s) cutting in and out).

CAUTION : Check that there are no coolant leaks.

# 4.2. Diesel engine Euro 6

The cutting in of the fan assembly for 10 seconds indicates the switch to after sales degas mode.   
Accelerate to an engine speed above 2300 rpm for more than 10 seconds to switch to degas mode.   
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 rpm until the fan assembly cuts in again.

4.3. Degassing and checking the cooling system (continued)

CAUTION : Check that the level of coolant in the filling cylinder is sufficient.

Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Do not remove the filling cylinder while the engine is hot.

Leave the engine to cool.   
Blank the filling cylinder using the blocking rod .   
Remove the filling cylinder , plug and adapter assembly.   
Check the coolant level when cold.   
Top up the coolant to the "max" level (Cold).

CAUTION : Do not fill the system past the max mark.

Refit and tighten the cap on the header tank .

CAUTION : Check that the cooling system filler cap is locked (For bayonet cap).

# 4. Operation check

Method of operation :

Switch off ignition and restart 3 times

# 2. Forced regeneration of the particle emission filter

ESSENTIAL : Respect the safety and cleanlinessrecommendations that are speific t high pressure diesel ijection (HDi) engines.

ESSENTIALheedti ileca hfthai tieerkshpara hardstagand ote frm an mableaterialake the work areseure.Ensureat ne passtand beind th veicldg the foratiPut thicteg" poi(iei peiCekteersol lproducts inside the boot. Wear heat-resistant gloves. Connect the vehicle to an approved gas extractor for this type of operation.

CAUTION : Check that the level of fuel in the tank is sufficient (minimum 20 litres).

CAUTION : Check the following fluid levels : Engine oil ; Coolant.

CAUTION : Check : The tightness of the turbocharging hoses (Risk of uncoupling).

ESSENTIAL : Remove the under-engine protection.

Start the engine and allow it to warm up (65°C minimum). Connect the diagnostic tool on the vehicle's central socket. Carry out :

Fault reading (Engine ECU) Fault clearing

Trigger the particle emission filter forced regeneration cycle ; Using the diagnostic equipment.   
After the regeneration cycle : Alow the engine to run at idle, with the bonnet open, to help the cooling.   
Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Wait at least one hour before carring out any work on the exhaust line. Wear heat-resistant gloves.

Refit the under-engine protection .

# 1. Application

This procedure applies to all ready-to-use batteries.   
They are fitted on new vehicles or sold as Replacement Parts (boutique, warehouse, gondola end.….).   
The batteries must guarantee quality and reliability which meet the requirements of our customers.   
They are an addition to the new vehicle preparation ranges distributed for each model of the range.

# 2. Recommended tools

Approved charging equipment : See garage equipment catalogue or, failing this, obtain a limited voltage charger.   
Approved battery cable.

# 3. General principles for charging batteries

Comply with the maximum voltage indications and the nominal current level in relation to the type and size of the battery

Never apply an excessive voltage or current   
Use a charger suited to the battery and the type of charge required   
Do not use a rapid charger or, if the charger has this function, use the normal charge function   
Check the condition of the battery

N.B. : The effectiveness of the charge depends on the condition of the battery.

# 4. Precautions to be taken

Do not charge :

A faulty battery (White hydrometer)   
A battery coated with sulphate (Depositing of a superficial layer of lead sulphate on the plates)   
A warm battery (Risk of thermal racing and damage)

# 3. ACEA standaras

3.1. Petrol and diesel mixed oils recommended by PSA

The meaning of the first letter does not change, it always refers to the engine type :

A = Petrol and petrol/LPG dual fuel engines B= diesel engines

The next figure does change and refers to the following types of oil :

3 = High performance oils   
4 = Oils specific to certain direct injection diesel engines   
5 = Oils with very high performance, favouring lower fuel consumption

Examples :

ACEA A3/B3 : Huiles mixtes hautes performances et bicarburation essence/GPL ACEA A5/B5 : Blended oils with very high performance, for all engines, favouring fuel economy

CAUTIONSi2004 eACEaoeiA,,.ee, liPrTh are no longer any oils specific to petrol or diesel.

# 3.2. Introduction of low ash content oils (LOW SAPS)

Oils with low ash content reduce the amount of particles etering theehaust and so help legthen the life ofthe particlefiter.   
The ash content changes from 1,3 % in current oils to 0,8 % in these new oils (maximum permitted values).

N.B. : LOW SAPS (Sulphated Ash Phosphorus Sulphur).

New specifications ACEA :

C3 : Moderate ash content • C2 : Moderate ash content and fuel economy C1 : Very low ash content and fuel economy

# 4. API oil standards

The meaning of the first letter does not change, it always refers to the engine type :

S = Petrol and petrol/LPG dual fuel engines C = diesel engines

The second letter corresponds to the evolution level of the oil (in rising order).   
Example : The standard SL is stricter than the standard SJ and corresponds to an improved level of performance.

Press the locking clip (2).   
Pull the clip (3) by one notch in the direction of the arrow (Position open).   
Action the clutch pedal manually through its entire travel rapidly 7 times.   
Leave the clutch pedal at the lower end of its travel during the last manoeuvre.   
Push back the clip (3) (closed position).   
Allow the clutch pedal to rise to the upper position.   
Fill the brake fluid reservoir to its maximum capacity.   
Press the locking clip (2).   
Pull the clip (3) by one notch in the direction of the arrow (Position open).   
Action the clutch pedal manually through its entire travel rapidly 7 times.   
Keep the clutch pedal at the lower end of its travel during the last manoeuvre.   
Push back the clip (3) (Closed position).   
Uncouple the transparent pipe.   
Top up the brake fluid level to the MAX. level in the brake fluid reservoir.   
Press the clutch pedal rapidly 40 times.   
Lower the vehicle.   
Start the engine.   
Apply the handbrake.   
Engage a gear. Check that clutch mechanism friction begins at a dimension "A" of 40 mm or more (the dimension (A) is given as a guide).   
Repeat the bleed operations (if necessary).

# 6. Gear wheels

The gear wheels have HCR (High Contact Ratio) helocoidal teeth. The lubrication of the gear trains and moving plants inside the gearbox is dynamic. The oil taken through openings and ducts on the hollow secondary shafts means :

Better efficiency the transmission of the torque and significantly reduced wear Good manoeuvrability at a low temperature through the use of a multigrade synthetic oil

# 6.1. Synchronizers

The synchronizers have floating rings made of brass (Type BORG-WARNER). Arrangements : Synchronizers :

The reverse gear, 3rd and 4th gear synchronizers are on the upper secondary shaft The synchronizers of 1st, 2nd, 5th and 6th gears are on the lower secondary shaft

CAUTION : Replace the driveshaf lip seals  .

Check for the absence of leaks on the following components :

Hydraulic clutch stop Crankshaft seal , Input shaft outlet seal

Check the state of wear of the clutch.   
Replace the clutch (If necessary).   
Clean the input shaft and the stop guide by hand using a wire brush to eliminate any traces of oxidation.   
Protect the interior of the clutch housing from splashes of grease.

N.B. : Apply KLUBERPASTE 46MR401 grease evenly to the input shaft.

Remove the surplus grease on the top of the grooves and the end of the input shaft using a cloth.

N.B. : An excess of grease wil cotaminate the clutch friction plate and cause noise in neutral, sipping or juddering of the clutch.

CAUTION : If the clutch disc is reused, the disc hub must be free of traces of oxidation.

Modification of the primary shafts greasing procedure.

CAUTION : Excessive greasing of the primary shaft may damage the clutch system as a result of splashes of grease.

# 2. Procedure to be followed : Greasing method

CAUTIONlaeaalealiea hand brush.

N.B. : Protect the interior of the clutch housing from splashes of grease.

CAUTIONeceseiiteuiitacaueutral ipi jihche grease from the splines of the primary shaft using a clean cloth.

2.1. Vehicles equipped with a gearbox that has a mechanical clutch bearing   
Spray alitle grease MOLYCOTE G-RAPID PLUS (aerosol) on the splines of the primary shaft and on the clutch bearing guide tube . 2.2. Vehicles equipped with a gearbox that has a hydraulic clutch bearing   
Grease the splines of the primary shaft with Kluberpaste 46 MR 401.

# 4. Checking the power steering pump

=ill the power steering fluid reservoir to the maximum level.

N.B. : Power steering fluid : TUTELLA GI/E.

Open the three-way tap [0710-C].   
Turn the steering mechanism from lock to lock several times.   
Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level.   
Start the engine.   
Check that there are no leaks.

CAUTION : Do not close the three-way tap [0710-C] for longer than 10 seconds

Close the three-way tap [0710-C].

Read the pressure value indicated on the pressure gauge as soon as the fluid stops from escaping. The pressure should be :

114 to 4 bars (2,2 litre engine)   
115 to 5 bars (3 litre engine)

Open the three-way tap [0710-C].   
Stop the engine.   
Pressure not correct : Replace the power steering pump.   
Power steering pump pressure correct : The problem comes from the steering mechanism.

N.B. : After confirming an actual lack of power-assistance (by prior test), change the power steering mechanism.

# 1. Drain and refill

Unscrew the power steering reservoir cap .   
Raise the vehicle and support on axle stands, wheels free.

![](images/4913b3f61e1d08a7c24500e179f2b21ff45799ec3d89df88bcdd925adfb01b34.webp)

Figure : B3FP7NUD

Uncouple the low pressure pipe union (1).   
Turn the steering in both directions, from lock to lock.   
Recover the power steering fluid.   
Plug the low pressure pipe union (1).

N.B. : Do not re-use the power steering fluid.

# 2. Refilling

Use fresh power steering fluid Oil quality : TUTELLA GI/E.

![](images/ff530fc27bc545d7e82f7c9f21e25ddec0a4b5ec54aa1590703140b17c076184.webp)  
Figure : B3EP19CD

"A" : Power steering fluid level when cold (20 °C).   
"B" : Power steering fluid level when warm (90 °C).   
Fill the power steering fluid reservoir to the maximum level.

# 3. Bleeding

N.B. : Return the vehicle to its wheels.

Engine stopped :

Fil the power steering fluid reservoir to the maximum level (If necessary) •Turn the steering in both directions, from lock to lock (3 times minimum) Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level (If necessary)

engine running :

Wait one minute Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level (If necessary) Move the steering from lock to lock, until there is no point of resistance

Stop the engine.   
Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level.   
Check there are no leaks.

# 1. recommendations

CAUTION : The use of impact wrenches to refit the wheel bolts and wheel antitheft bolts is strictly prohibited.

CAUTION : The wheels are always tightened with dry bolts.

CAUTION : When installig a new steel wheel for the first time, Always double tighten the wheel, t avoid any risk of slackening.

N.B. : Double ttening consist of tenng to the speified torque follwed by slackening then retgtening to the speified torque.

Ensure that the anti-theft wrench is positioned correctly on refiting.

CAUTION : Tighten the wheel bolts using a torque wrench.

# 3. Wheel valve

3.1. Vehicles not equipped with tyre under-inflation detection system Always replace the wheel valves when changing the tyres.

CAUTION : Vehicles DS3 Racing ; Tighten the wheel valves to 0,4 daNm.

3.2. Vehicles fitted with a tyre under-inflation detection system Observe the tightening torque of the wheel valve nuts : Tighten to 0,8 daN.m.

# REPLACEMENT : FRONT HALF-PANEL ASSEMBLY

ESSENTIAL : Allof the stripped surfaces must be protected by means of the approved electrolytic rezincing process (see the relevant operations).

# 3.2. Applying the adhesive

Fit the extruder gun with the mastic mixer assembly.   
Take the nozzle supplied in the glueing kit.   
Cut out the end of the nozzle to a diameter of 8 mm and a height of 13 mm.   
1st case : windscreen (Recovered).   
There is no need to apply primer.   
The bearing face for affixing seal must be perfectly clean.   
Remove any impurities on the shaved seal ; Using a blow gun .   
2nd case : windscreen (New).   
Degrease the glass surround using the product selected from the bonding kit.   
Further primer must be applied fllowing the line of the primer applied during manufacture (Allow to dry for 10 mn).

CAUTION : No more than 8 minutes must elapse between applying the mastic and positioning the glass (For the quicl setting bonding mastics).

Apply the bead of adhesive to the centre of the trace of primer.

CAUTION : Do not apply stress to the windscreen.

Position a strap on the tools [KIT1-VENT] to keep the windscreen in contact.   
Allow to cure for 30 minutes before handling.   
Check the sealing of the windscreen.

# 3. Cleaning

3.1. Preparing the quarter window

Re-use of the quarter window :

Fit the electric knife [FEIN-400E] with the blade N°146 • Remove the adhesive sealing bead Remove any dust using a clean cloth Only apply the primer to the zones laid bare 0

Fitting a new quarter window :

Degrease the edge of the quarter window ; Using the degreaser Apply the glass primer provided in the bonding kit part number "A3"

N.B. : Only apply the primer to the zones laid bare.

# 3.2. Preparation of the aperture

On the remains of the bead of sealing adhesive :

Fit the electric knife [FEIN-400E] with the blade N°146

JUMPER IlC5CG0108P0 - Removing - reftting : Rear quarter window

Remove the adhesive sealing bead Remove any dust using a clean cloth

On the new component :

Degrease the aperture   
Apply the metal primer provided in the bonding kit part number "A3"   
Allow to dry for 10 mn

Lightly press on the periphery of the rear quarter window (3).

ESSENTIAL : Observe the vehicle immobilisation time following fiting of the windscreen recommended by the suppliers of the products used.

# REPAIR : IMPACT ON THE LAMINATED WINDOWS PRINCIPLES OF REPAIR

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations  .

1. Tooling   
1 Repair kit (Manual injection ).   
1 Repair kit (Injection using the pressure/vacuum pump ).

N.B. : Refer to the tools catalogue.

# 2. Windscreen repair area

CAUTION : Read the repair manual in full.

![](images/8f46553105a9240bdf9ee8c43373b3e6d5edc30add1f7c9e9ed6a68a20fd209d.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06WD

"A" = 300 mm.

ESSENTIAL : The repair of a windscreen in the field of vision of the driver, see "A", is prohibited.

ESSENTIAL : If the impact is more than 50 mm : Replace the windscreen.

# 3. Types of impact

# 3.1. Bubble or half-bubble impacts

![](images/d240b672b7fc2986378af29e70b2e6a2dc5b02fc43e17c6a99be1bf00f626021.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06XD

"B" = 20 mm (Max ).

N.B. : Formation of a small hole at the point of impact and a core in the form of a cone is created.

3.2. Star impact

![](images/597de634351b3c6d72748b7c4b97cf774bb65e41c54e3120ecb9ee22eb84d9c0.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06YD

"C" = 50 mm (Max ).   
Formation of cracks or worse, spreading from the point of impact.

3.3. Star bubble or combination impact

![](images/666371358d163168d8b77db2590a04afb772b7b397dc6a9f980b5f87dbbf83ee.webp)  
Figure : C5CM08PD

"D" = 50 mm (Max ).   
Formation of cracks or worse, spreading from the point of impact.

# 4. Precautions regarding use

N.B. : Numerous factors can affect the result of a repair.

The most important points to be complied with are the following :

Check for the presence of moisture in the impact Check that the temperature of the window is between 10°C and 30°C Protect the resin from ultraviolet rays   
• Control the amount of pressure during the injection of the impact

# 4.1. Humidity

N.B. : If moisture is present, dry out the impact using the heating lamp.

CAUTION : Heat the laminated window moderately using the heating lamp as any other excessively strong anc excessively violent heat source may enlarge the impact and crack the laminated window.

# 4.2. Temperature

The ideal temperature for repairing a laminated window is between 10°C and 30°C.

4.3. Ultraviolet rays Repair away from ultraviolet rays.

4.4. Pressure

Follow the pressure level recommendations in the repair manual.

5. Repair

N.B. : Proceed in the same way for an athermic windscreen.

Place a protective cloth on the bonnet for setting down the tools.   
Clean the laminated window around the impact using a dry, lint-free cloth.

N.B. : Do not spray any products onto the impact.

5.1. Fitting

Glass scratch repair kit.

# 2. Windscreen repair area

CAUTION : Read the repair manual in full.

![](images/60d542f106668a8f9bc54cddf2bc75935715c98c5bfb91574a95d54f9e4f4e72.webp)  
Figure : C5CM095D

# 3. Precautions regarding use

N.B. : Always store the discs in individual plastic bags to avoid contamination. Excessive heat may break the glass.

JUMPER II - C5CM0106P0 - Repair : Scratch on glass

ESSENTIAL : Keep the temperature of the glass under control to prevent it from breaking.

Mixing 5 litres of distilled water with the dose provided permits several repairs of optimum quality. If the polisher bounces on the glass during the operation, increase the level of water and the angle of the polisher slightly.

ESSENTIAL : Use the polisher with extreme care (Splashes of water).

# 4. Scratch

CAUTION : A scratch which can be detected with a fingernail is considered deep and therefore irreparable.

Repairable scratches : Slight scratches Very slight scratches

ESSENTIAL : Follow the repair process using the discs is descending order, blue, orange and white.

# 5. Preparation

![](images/ad78a36e9c9253d9d6ed3120fe512a2c3a0ce7757886d99f03a13e422ecee763.webp)  
Figure : C5CM096D

Examine the scratch (at "a") to be repaired and determine its repair.

N.B. : To see the surface to be worked on more easily, mark the interior of the window using a black marker.

Clean the glass.

Protect the vehicle against slashes of water.

# ESSENTIAL : Use distilled water.

Fill the water reservoir with the full dose provided for 5 litres of water.   
Pump the coolant reservoir several times to pressurise it.   
The pipe must be connected to the polisher.   
Check that the red water flow valve is in the closed position.

![](images/3001f48f805e4524512a507d6ae4ebd4de6626b22a19d264c7ad8aad9c0ab460.webp)  
Figure : C5CM097D

# 5.1. Polishing

CAUTION : Too litle water may result in an increase in the temperature of the polishing disc and shorten its service life; too much water slows down the polishing process.

'urn the valve anticlockwise until a few drops of water begin to flow from the centre of the polishing head

ESSENTIAL : Follow the repair process using the discs is descending order, blue, orange and white.

Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be polished.   
Eliminate the scratch (at "a") ; Using the polisher.   
Polish the area (at "b").   
Clean the glass ; Using a scraper.   
Visually check the progress of the repair.   
After a few minutes of polishing, the scratch begins to disappear.   
Continue polishing until the scratch has disappeared completely.

# 5.2. Final polishing

There are 2 options for the final polishing stage.

1 option :

Use the white disc ; Using the polisher   
Increase the flow and quantity of water   
Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be repaired   
Polish the area (at "b")   
If the polisher begins to bounce, increase the flow of water   
Continue the final polish, until a satisfactory result is achieved

2 option :

Use the foam disc ; Using the polisher Apply the polishing fluid or powder to the foam disc Add a few drops of water to the foam Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be repaired Polish the area (at "b") Continue the final polish, until a satisfactory result is achieved • If cloudy marks remain after polishing, Use option 1 to achieve a satisfactory result

# LOCATION : COLD STAMPING OF THE SERIAL NUMBER (VIN)

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations  .

ESSENTIAL : Observe the precautions to be taken for the pre-tensioning components

ESSENTIAL : Before any work on the structure of a vehicle with on board electric energy (electric vehicle/hybrid vehicle), the vehicle must be isolated by an authorised technician. Only those personnel that have received training specific to electric or hybrid vehicles are qualified to work on the vehicle's electrical system.

# 1. Characteristics of the serial number

The regulation size of the punches for cold stamping is 7 mm.   
The serial number consists of 17 characters.   
The serial number is always situated on the right-hand section of the vehicle.   
Depending on the vehicle, the serial number may be stamped on 1 or 2 lines. "a" Original punch.   
Each line forming a serial number must have a non alphanumeric character "a" at each end.

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations  .

ESSENTIAL : Observe the precautions to be taken for the pre-tensioning components

ESSENTIAL : Before any work on the structure of a vehicle with on board electric energy (electric vehicle/hybrid vehicle), the vehicle must be isolated by an authorised technician.

CAUTION : Allof the stripped surfaces must be protected by means of the approved electrolytic rezincing process .

# 1. Legislation

CAUTION : Refer to the regulations in force in the country.

2. Cold stamping is possible in the following cases

# 2.1. Case n°1

Replacement of the part bearing the cold stamped serial number.   
Absence of the cold stamped serial number.

# 2.2. Case n°2

No visual access following modification not foreseen by the manufacturer.   
Serial number illegible due to considerable corrosion.   
Serial number concealed (Addition of products).   
Traces of work in the serial number area (Symmetrical welding and grinding).

# 3. Information

# 3.1. Characteristics of the serial number

The regulation size of the punches for cold stamping is 7 mm.   
The serial number consists of 17 characters.   
The serial number is always situated on the right-hand section of the vehicle.   
Depending on the vehicle, the serial number may be stamped on one or two lines.   
In all cases, the serial number must be cold stamped onto a structural part.

3.2. Specifications for cold stamping of the serial number (VIN) in service

![](images/eb6eb5c0cfb95a0703ede325ff88ed2b6f65f445678723c073f623ec2e9422d2.webp)  
Figure : C4EBONKD

"a" Non alphanumeric character.   
When cold stamping, the marque punch mark is not compulsory.   
Each line forming a serial number must have the symbol "a" at each end.

3.3. Creating the symbol

![](images/42156ac3689e3d6004456fa182e8038b3795d76dac51fdb59c0a1a5233e9db9f.webp)

Figure : C4EBONLD

The symbol "a" is obtained by stamping the letter "X" placed horizontally, with a second stamping of the letter "I" superimposed. The cold stamping of a serial number must be carred out by an authorised repairer of the manufacturer's marque.

# 4. Tooling

Kit of 7 mm stamping punches.   
Mechanic's hammer . Coachbuilder's dolly .   
Use the dolly to prevent any distortion of the panel during stamping.   
Position the dolly on the opposite face of the cold stamping area.

![](images/eab315b433d9e0d15b86c0d9660191b5e67f27a85cb3df99ac4a2ccd424da26a.webp)  
Figure : E5AB16TD

# 5. Preliminary operations

CAUTION : To prevent any corrosion, the cold stamping must be carried out before painting.

Remove the components necessary for positioning the coachbuilder's dol and the stamping punches.

6. Cold stamped inscription

N.B. : 2 operators are required for this operation.

7. Cold stamping of the serial number (VIN)

JUMPER IlC4EB016JPO - Cold stamped inscription : Serial number (VIN) in after sale

CAUTION : The serial number is always situated on the right-hand section of the vehicle.

The serial number can be stamped close to the original one, whether underneath, above or to the side.   
Refer to the method : Location  : Cold stamping of the serial number (VIN).   
The stamping of the serial number (VIN) may require removal of a component (Windscreen, scutle grile, bulkhead protection, etc.).

# 8. Protection

Apply a phosphate-print layer on the zone laid bare.   
Paint as required.

# 9. Refitting

Refit the items removed beforehand (Windscreen, scuttle grile, bulkhead protection, etc.).

# TECHNICAL NOTE : BLEEDING THE BRAKE SYSTEM

CAUTION : The use of DOT4 brake fluid for the brake circuits is compulsory.

CAUTION : During the bleeding operation : Keep the fluid topped up in the reservoir and complete it.

N.B. : Use only clean fluid free from bubbles. Avoid any introduction of impurities into the hydraulic system.

# 1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit

CAUTION : Do not switch on the ignition at any time during the operation.

N.B. : Bleed the primary circuit until clean, non-foaming brake fluid is obtained.

There are 2 procedures for bleeding the primary brake circuit.

1.1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit (With the bleeding device) Bleed the circuit following the instructions for use of the equipment.

1.2. Bleeding the primary braking circuit (without brake bleeding equipment)

N.B. : Two operators are necessary.

Couple a transparent tube on the bleed screw .   
Press the brake pedal slowly.   
Open the bleed screw .   
Hold the pedal fully down.   
Close the bleed screw .   
Allow the brake pedal to return naturally.   
Repeat the operation until the fluid running out is clean and free from air bubbles.   
Proceed in the same way for the other wheels.

N.B. : Check that the wheels rotate freely when the parking brake is released .

# 1.3. Checking : Bleeding the primary braking circuit

At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the travel of the brake pedal (no extension).   
If the travel is long and spongy, repeat the bleed procedure.   
Start the engine.   
Check the travel of the brake pedal (no extension) ; Road test the vehicle (if necessary).   
If brake pedal travel is not correct ; Bleed the secondary brake circuit.

# 2. Bleed the secondary brake circuit

Bleeding of the secondary braking circuit is done with a diagnostic tool.   
This procedure is only carried out if the primary brake circuit has been bled.   
Continue the procedure for bleeding of the hydraulic circuit as defined by the diagnostic tool.   
At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the brake pedal travel (no extension), otherwise repeat the bleeding procedure.

# 3. Front brake disc

Check the tightening torques of the wheels.

A dial gauge zero reset A full turn of the brake disc

# 2. Preliminary operation

Untighten the rear wheel bolts.   
Raise and support the vehicle, with the rear wheels hanging free.   
Remove the rear wheels.

![](images/dbb63173a42cf527d8bfbf01b0e23cf3a01af69a47188add4e39aa906c54e294.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KND

Remove :

The rear brake pads (see the relevant operation) The bolts (1)

Move aside and suspend the brake caliper (2).

3. Checking the thickness

![](images/539d3bcbe3757cd869f4e79c9ea52f87885b8c6d2a877a458831e529117bbb8a.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KPD

Use a 0/50 mm micrometer.   
Max. thickness variation on one circumference = 0,025 mm .   
Nominal thickness : 15,9/16,2 mm .   
Min. permissible thickness (wear) : 14,2 mm .   
Always replace the discs that are not as thick as the value shown.   
In the case of damage or deep scratches, the surfaces of the disc may be ground.   
Minimum permitted thickness after grinding : 14,55 mm .

4. Checking the run-out

![](images/ec7b082be4cd9a485bf5eef7be0366c5c4742997fb263d38321def5aac83bee7.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7KQD

Fix the magnetic support [1] on the spring leaf.   
Attach the dial gauge [2] to the magnetic bracket [1].   
The brake disc run-out check is carried out at approximately 2 mm from the outside diameter.   
Turn the brake disc by a full rotation.   
Maximum run-out = 0,030 mm .

5. Brake disc inside diameter check

![](images/5a9eab6929977d63c8347727a06e6f0c6d75b877c0a0765c375bd2644965f76a.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7K7D

Remove :

The bolts (3) The rear brake disc

![](images/81355c4f828a30a84b6e68f10d4f6f595213a47f64095bc9669edef8a8525ed5.webp)

Figure : B3FP7KRD

A : Disc brake bore diameter : Nominal diameter : 172/172,15 mm Maximum permitted diameter after wear : 173 mm

Brake shoe lining : Min. permissible thickness = 1,5 mm .

# 6. Additional operations

Refit : The rear brake disc The bolts (3)

Tighten the bolts (3) to 1,2 ± 0,1 daN.m.   
Position the brake caliper (2).   
Refit the bolts (1) (new) (pre-coated with a thread locking product).   
Tighten the bolts (1) to 16 ± 0,5 daN.m.   
Fit the brake pads (see the relevant operation).   
Apply the brakes, with the engine running, several times before driving the vehicle.   
Check the operation of the brakes.   
Refit the rear wheels.   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten the wheel bolts  .

CAUTION : Brake fluid is toxic. Avoid contact with the skin and the eyes. In the event of contact with the eyes, rinse them immediately with copious amounts of water for several minutes.

CAUTION : Brake fluid is highly corosive to paintwork. If any is projected onto the bodywork, clean the surface immediately.

# 1. Stop lamp switch (With manual adjustment)

# 1.1. Removing

Disconnect the connector of the stop lamp switch (1).   
Rotate the stop lamp switch (1) a quarter turn to the left to unlock it.   
Take out the stop lamp switch (1).

# 1.2. Refitting

CAUTION : Make sure that the brake pedal is in the rest position and that it remains so throughout the operation.

Make sure that the locking latch "a" on the push rod support "b" is inside the extension of the stop lamp switch centring lug (1).

If this is so, the travel of the plunger support "b" within the brake light switch (1) is limited.   
Present the stop lamp switch (1) to its support, with the thrust pad "c" against the brake pedal.   
Pressfirmly on the brake light witch ) in the centreline to set the piston"" in the plungersupport "" until the base of the brake light switch (1) is in contact with its support.   
Rotate the stop lamp switch (1) a good quarter turn to the right to lock it.   
Reconnect the connector of the stop lamp switch (1).   
Switch on the ignition.   
Check that the brake lights come on.

1.3. Check the adjustment : Stop lamp switch (Brake pedal at rest)

![](images/2ed0b3d02a10dba0d4cc977e078d8a8513e840db6092637a2a89a2684087e1b8.webp)  
Figure : B3FG248D

Check the position of the plunger support "b" in the brake light switch (1).   
The plunger support "b" should be flush with the body of the brake light switch (1) and the plunger "c" should be in contact with the brake pedal.

N.B. : The brake light switch (1) must not be used as a stop for the brake pedal.

1.4. Check the adjustment : Stop lamp switch (Brake pedal pressed down)

![](images/cfe2f1c7559af76e052e825884eff6286a40d41947d85fce4e26602d6f546d1d.webp)  
Figure : B3FG249D

The push rod support "b" is free and the push rod "c" is no longer is contact with the brake pedal .

ESSENTIAL : Do not use compressed air to clean the brakes.

3.2. 2nd possibility

# 3. Bleeding the brake system

CAUTION : During the bleeding operation : Keep the fluid topped up in the reservoir and complete it. Use new brake fluid only.

Bleed the primary brake circuit during a conventional operation. Bleed the secondary brake circuit in the following cases :

Venting the secondary brake circuit Starting the pump supply to the electrovalves

![](images/0c465f000db9ff83a9d6251d00bd3a4588538a5b30ca7a05ed519f651fc21865.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7N9D

front brake caliper : bleed screw(s) (2).

Figure : B3FP7NAD

rear brake caliper : bleed screw(s) (3).

3.1. Bleeding the primary braking circuit

CAUTION : The ABS system must not be in operation during the bleeding procedure.

Use a bleed tool approved by the manufacturer.

![](images/2495057cfcf734072745d8e070b168fa5c1635aeee466c5e4470856770d22721.webp)  
Figure : B1BPRWAD

Connect the bleeding apparatus [/] on the brake fluid reservoir . Set the pressure of the equipment to 2 bars. Bleeding order :

• RH rear • Left hand front • Left hand rear , Right hand front

![](images/13391e0e6c576058d964c2b512169730f8dd8d08f4fe695abf8bc06ec365c82f.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7NBD

CAUTION : Proceed bolt by bolt in the order shown.

Perform the following operations :

Couple a transparent pipe (4) to the bleed screw   
Submerge the other end of the tube into a clean receptacle   
Open the bleed screw   
Wait for the liquid to flow without air bubbles   
Close the bleed screw Remove the bleeding equipment .   
Check the brake fluid level (between the "MIN" level and the "MAX" level).   
If necessary, fill with approved and recommended synthetic brake fluid.

CAUTION : Any operation which may cause the pump to start or energize electrovalves is to be avoided (the systen has been pre-filled and bled).

# 3.2. Bleed the secondary brake circuit (ABS/ESP hydraulic block)

N.B. : The equipment to be bled is always connected to the brake fluid reservoir.

Select a diagnostic tool.   
Connect the diagnostic tool.   
From the screen of the diagnostic tool, select the menu : "ABS PURGE".   
Follow the instructions on the diagnostic tool.   
Bleed the brakes observing the order indicated (ABS type bleeding operation).   
At the end of the bleed programme, check and top up, if necessary, the brake fluid level.   
Check the brake pedal travel (no extension), otherwise repeat the bleeding procedure.   
Remove the tools.

SVG Viewer Tools History

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

# 1. Recommended tools

Glazing consumable  .

![](images/50b2cfc8de447a3fd5f49ea51116e2a77992a30c05083565c33ae4227d8c6aff.webp)  
Figure : E5AP2ZQD

[1] Bonded windows removal kit (-).1354. Composition of the toolkit :

[1a] Guide roller device   
•[1b] Awl [1c] Guiding roller [1d] Square section cutting wire   
[1e] handle [2] electric knife.   
[3] shovel blade N° 146.

![](images/aa40f3eb23cccdeb6862b9dacb0ce99221561fe1271af42f83717e57b36996d0.webp)  
Figure : E5AP2ZRD

![](images/5f00cc8358de5b09a3d99b966ff84c0c3e09d46ce003c766151bd699d3f358cb.webp)  
Figure : E5AP30AD

[4] Pneumatic gun (For one part cartridge).

[5] Electric gun (For two-part cartridge).

![](images/d6eb1eb18dd517d75cb76c3bf52dd9957401b8618c6e048dea9f6b73b03996de.webp)  
Figure : E5AP2ZTD

[6] Articulated suction pads (Part number 9776.Y0).

2. Removing

![](images/a67d6705b117fd01209525cc7064314bc1908857a820acb6a1416391fc07d854.webp)  
Figure : C4BMOERD

N.B. : If the window is to be reused, align it and affix adhesive tape (1)(at "a").

Unplug : The 2 de-icing connectors (Rear door window).

![](images/43fefd4ef91084ee11b19edaf8537dd013b2d645be10ef50260a08c18dd74610.webp)  
Figure : C4BM0ESD

JUMPER Il - C4BGo10SP0 - Removing - refiting : Hinged rear door glass

Install the handles [1e] at each end of the cutting wire [1d].   
Pass the cutting wire [1d] as indicated on the diagram (Behind the window).

CAUTION : 2 operators are necessary to carry out the following operations.

Cut the bead of adhesive by means of a to-and-fro movement of the cutting wire [1d].   
When cutting, the indexing pins must be cut.

N.B. : The indexing pins are not necessary for refitting.

Remove : The rear door window (2) ; Using the double hinged suction cups [6].

3. Cleaning

3.1. Preparation : Rear door window

Reuse of the rear door window :

Fit the electric knife [2] with the blade [3] Remove the adhesive sealing bead • Remove any dust using a clean cloth

CAUTION : Only apply the primer to the zones laid bare .

Fitting of a new rear door window :

Degrease the edge of the glass with the degreaser Apply the glass primer provided in the bonding kit part number "A3"

CAUTION : Only apply the primer to the zones laid bare .

# 3.2. Preparation of the aperture

On the remains of the bead of sealing adhesive :

Fit the electric knife [2] with the blade [3] , Remove the adhesive sealing bead • Remove any dust using a clean cloth

On the new component :

Degrease the aperture Apply the metal primer provided in the bonding kit part number "A3" 0   
Allow to dry for 10 mn

# 4. Refitting

4.1. Reuse of the rear door window

![](images/ebf4e92260398b4631c8922e4655e151379d29af48a114f47ace3e47ac58d0d3.webp)  
Figure : C5CM01XD

"A" = 12 mm .   
"B" = 8 mm .   
Cut the nozzle in triangular section to obtain a bead of sealing adhesive "B" wide and "A" deep.

ESSENTIAL : Always replace : The faulty seals.

Apply a bead of sealing adhesive to the periphery of the rear door window (2) (using tools [4] or [5]) (at "").

ESSENTIAL : Use of the two part product: the time for fitting the window on the vehicle and the start of extrusion of the sealing adhesive is 5 minutes.

Refit the rear door window :

Using the double hinged suction cups [6] Using adhesive tapes (1)

Press lightly on the periphery of the rear door window (2).   
Clean the rear door window and its surround.

4.2. Fitting of a new rear door window

![](images/5b8dd70ce3ac6f28b03b8987b380ee6a4591a5e7eee8edd59a3cc5968c006d3f.webp)  
Figure : C4BMOETD

Test fit the rear door window (2).   
Position the adhesive strips (1).   
Cut the tape ( as "a").   
Remove : The rear door window (2).   
Apply a bead of sealing adhesive to the periphery of the rear door window (2) (at "b").

ESSENTIAL : Use of the two part product: the time for fitig the window on the vehicle and the start of extrusion of the sealing adhesive is 5 minutes.

Refit the rear door window :

Using the double hinged suction cups [6] Using adhesive tapes (1)

Press lightly on the periphery of the rear door window (2).   
Clean the rear door window and its surround.

ESSENTIAL : Observe the vehicle immobilisation time following fiting of the windscreen recommended by the suppliers of the products used.

Continue the fitting operations in the reverse order to removal.   
Check the sealing of the rear door window (2).   
Clean the rear door window and its surround.   
Check the electrical operation of the equipment.

# 1. Recommended tools

![](images/cd902479b9edcdff0f313f273456c980aea30b928071b1ff8c92b10bfefa00e2.webp)  
Figure : E5AP2WXD

[1] mobile support for door positioning.

# 2. Removing

Strip the front door (see the relevant operation).

![](images/6a0fdf55f87dd43830cb461ef155085dbf5f6cead18611f45f753a61f073a888.webp)  
Figure : C5FP0Y2D

Remove :

The bolts (1 - 2 - 3) The front door (4) ; Using tool [1]

# 3. Refitting

Proceed in the reverse order to removal.   
Check the electric operation.

Tighten :

The bolts (2 - 3) to 2,5 ± 0,2 daN.m The bolts (1) to 0,8 ± 0,3 daN.m

# 4. Adjustment

Fit and clearance values (see the relevant operation).

![](images/9f5c16373c5a5767e2030b6d2384be2c6591a72bb042a0d5286ae18d70ac9087.webp)  
Figure : C4CP1PUD

A : Door upper adjustment.   
B, C : Door adjustment.   
D : Door lower adjustment.

4.1. Door upper and lower adjustment (at "A" and "D")

![](images/1247a16f4a2b96ea60115ce5e927f587b050696fa1152e59e2fa5eca304bb608.webp)

Slacken the screws ( 5) one 1/4th of a turn.   
Position the front door hinge ( 6) to adjust the clearance of the door.   
Tighten the bolts (5). Slacken the screws ( 8) one 1/4th of a turn.   
Position the front door striker ( 7) to adjust the fit of the door.   
Tighten the bolts (8) to 2,5 ± 0,2 daN.m.

![](images/8ed10382a0993a5941cd877cb830d86918db9fbb2f8a3dfcaf8d78f5986ca6b8.webp)  
Figure : C4CP1PVD   
Figure : C4CP1PWD

4.2. Door adjustment (at "B" and "C")

![](images/490582f990d04280aa8603fa16aa66b67b464404896bba68ca005682f3e4fe97.webp)  
Figure : C5FP0Y3D

Slacken the screws ( 2 - 3) one 1/4th of a turn.   
Position the front door ( 4) to adjust the clearance and fit of the door.   
Tighten the bolts (2 - 3) to 2,5 ± 0,2 daN.m.

# 1. Recommended tools

![](images/d1833fbda6dfe070a273cb7b6300791619c80c2654a52866bfef343bdfb095b5.webp)  
Figure : E5AP2WMD

[ 1] set of door support stands 0207-T.

![](images/70fa603b38783c3554ba53b7f114523aa8b6cfa15fd8308f7dcb7c4a27456d98.webp)  
Figure : C4BP1P3D

Support the door (5) ; Using the stands.
