# 4. Adjustments

Fit and clearance values (see the relevant operation).

![](images/56222ff43a7986244eb650423aa33c26d16d9ec526dae6efdf5a37b776cf8ab7.webp)

4.1. Upper adjustment of the doors (at "a")

![](images/ef015f07855193cd5ab925b7c9e2674275ec4a042a623b76ecfdcce7c045efca.webp)

# 3. Refitting

3.1. Preparation of the flange and fixed window glass

To the electric knife [2] fit the blade [3] no. 146.   
Shave the beads of adhesive on the fixed window glass and the flange.   
Touch up with anti-corrosion product.   
Degrease the flange using the product selected from the adhesive kit.   
Allow to dry for 10 mn.

# 3.2. Applying the adhesive

![](images/4c787bd9febe3504ae4ffbb8fcd80e22dcaaa902e2590e4664ba570b4cef1dd3.webp)  
Figure : C5CP09PD

Place the mastic mixer assembly into the gun [5].   
Take the nozzle supplied in the glueing kit.   
Cut the nozzle to 8,0 mm dia. at 12 mm from the tip.   
1st case : The fixed window (Reused).   
There is no need to apply primer.   
Remove any impurities on the shaved seal ; Using a blow gun .   
2nd case : The fixed window (New).   
Degrease the surround of the glass with the products chosen from the bonding kit. The glass (2) is supplied pre-coated with primer .   
Further primer must be applied following the line of the primer applied during manufacture as "") (Allow to dry for 10 mn).

ESSENTIAL : No more than 8 minutes must elapse between applying the mastic and positioning the glass (For the quick setting bonding mastics).

Apply the bead of adhesive to the centre of the trace of primer ( as "c").

![](images/df5bf35b79e25054d88137a0741b96bb874abe8d20303004c553f22bde524665.webp)  
Figure : C5CP09QD

Position the fixed window glass ; Using the guides (3).   
Refit the guide fixings (1) to keep the glass in contact.   
Retain the glass in position ; Using tool [6].   
Allow to cure for 30 minutes before handling.   
Check : Check the sealing of the quarterlight by running water over it.   
Proceed in the reverse order to removal.

Connect the connector (at "a").

Refit : The rubber protection (according to equipment) . The front LH headlamp

Bleed the brake system .

Start communication by ECU.

To calibrate the longitudinal acceleration sensor, go to the replacement parts menu, switch module at the steering whe calibration of the steering wheel angle sensor (CAV).

# REPAIR : ELECTRICAL HARNESSES

The aim of this document is to define the rules for carrying out repairs or work on the electrical harnesses. This document consists of 2 main parts :

The first part describes the general repair methods The second part describes the circumstances of use of these methods in relation to the failures detecte

# 1. Recommendations prior to carrying out the operation

The repairs must only be carried out by trained and authorised personnel.

ESSENTIAL : Disconnect the battery before carring out any repairs or work on an electrical harness (electric battery ancilaries battery, traction battery, etc.).

ESSENTIAL : Take into account the manufacturer's instructions before carring out any work on the pyrotechnic functions (available on the computer equipment or on the marque's technical information internet site.

# 2. Tooling

![](images/1cca0ec907d308d5edc4fc4928a4db6748ca7a98dc7c841da708387a5f14bb38.webp)

![](images/5ff563a9665c8952d9b1d806427667472873834045c7f6464e830c858003de8c.webp)

# 3. Terminology

# 3.1. Usable wire

A wire is usable if is length i suficient to permit repair without causing any tensile stress which could alter the sealing the connection, the crimping resistance or result in a break over time (too taut).

N.B. : The wire is usable if its graspable length is more than 30 mm.

# 3.2. Unusable wire

A wire is unusable i its length is not suficient to permit repair without causing tensile stress which could alter the sealin! of the connection or result in a break over time (too taut). A wire is unusable if it is stripped, pulled out, crushed over a considerable length or burnt.

N.B. : The wire is unusable if its graspable length is less than 30 mm.

# 4. General rules

General rules to be heeded :

The repairs must only be carried out by trained and authorised personnel   
•After repair, all of the electrical functions affected by the harness must be checked   
The connection of 2 conductors by tin soldering is prohibited (rigidity, breakage)   
•The optical fibres and the screened wires must always be replaced if they are bent or broken   
After analysing the fault, eliminate its cause   
The twisted wires can be repaired

ESSENTIAL : Take into account the manufacturer's instructions before carrying out any work on the pyrotechnic functions (available on the computer equipment or on the marque's technical information internet site.

ESSENTIAL : Allrepairs or work on electrical harnesses are carried out with the battery disconnected Including the service battery if present).

# 5. Repair procedures

# 5.1. Method for checking a wire

The aim of the wire checking method is to determine whether the repair can be carried out directly on the damaged wire or whether part of the wire must be replaced.

A wire is declared unusable in the following cases :

The wire is not of suficient length to permit repair without causing traction stresses which could alter the sealing of the connection or breakage over time (too taut)   
The wire is stripped, pulled out or crushed over a considerable length   
The wire is burnt   
In the case of a wire leaving an overmoulded connector, f the remaining usable length of wire is lessthan 30 mm

N.B. : In other cases, the wire is declared usable.

# 5.2. Method for selecting a wire

If a wire is unusable, the choice of the new wire to be used to carr out the repair must conform to the follwing characteristics :

Cross-section of the wire Colour of the sleeve

ESSENTAL : The cross-section of the wire must be equal to or larger than the initial cross-section, but never smaller.

N.B. : Depending on certain factors, a larger wire cross-section may cause interference or even a reduction in current.

It is compulsory for an earth cable to be green and yellow.   
The other supply or information cables can be of a different colour.

N.B. : Favour the use of a cable of the same colour for the repair.

# 5.3. Method for stripping a wire

fer cuttin the wire, strip it without cutting the strands using approved wire strippers and observing the following length

2,8 ± 0,5 mm for crimping of a clip or MQS tab •5 ± 1 mm for crimping of a clip or MQS tab •8 ± 1 mm for crimping a sleeve 15 ± 1 mm for an insertion in a sleeve

# 5.4. Method for tin soldering

Thestrengthening of a faulty crimp (electrical resistance too high) by tin soldering is permited, observing the following procedure.

Tools required :

Soldering iron with clean bit Tin 0,7 mm (60% tin 40% lead) with soldering flux without halogen

Method of operation :

Melt a little tin on the iron bit   
Apply the iron bit under the crimp, the crimp wings must be visible   
Apply the tin wire to the copper strands at the end of the crimp (Soldering consumption approximately 3 mm)

N.B. : The times indicated are only valid for wires with a cross-section of 0,35 to 0,6 mm². For larger cross-sections increase the time by 2 to 3 seconds.

CAUTION : It is important not to apply too much ti (risk of stifening of the wire to avoid damaging the wire insulatior and the single-wire seals.

# 5.5. Method for unclipping a contact

ESSENTIAL : In extremely cold temperatures, the vehicle must be moved into a heated area and left to return to a temperature of approximately 20 °C before any work is carried out.

The contact must only be unclipped using the unclipping tool which is part of the approved kit and in accordance with instructions included.

CAUTION : Take care not to damage the seals, the contact cell, or the contacts to guarantee the sealing of th connector on refitting.

# 5.6. Method for selecting a contact

When replacing a contact or a spade terminal in a connector, it is imperative that the same components are used (gold plated or tin-plated clip).

5.7. Method for positioning a contact in its cell

![](images/1c4cc3721e8473f8b8dbdd6500415379a9417fe957b1795cfc7d6a5abb2e1161.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03RD

Positioning a contact :

Visually analyse the condition of the contact Insert the contact in its cell •Put the double lock back in place (according to equipment)

Pull the wire gently

CAUTION : If the contactis not retained in the cell, the connector must be replaced.

5.8. Method for applying a heat-shrink sleeve

![](images/ae65b748be702bae4f298ce852a23eacba4763f36b87e15b7bfb071b398ebfc5.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03SD

The heat-shrink sleeves must be chosen according to the cross-section of the wire to be repaired :

"a" Red sleeve : Wire between 0,35 mm2 and 1 mm2   
•"b" Blue sleeve : Wire between 1 mm2 and 3 mm2   
"c" Yellow sleeve : Wire between 3 mm2 and 5 mm2

N.B. : Crimp the heat-shrink sleeve using the tools and items in the connection repair kit. fthe repair requires the us of several heat-shrink sleeves, stagger them to retain a minimal volume.

# 5.9. Simple repair (1 Heat-shrink sleeve )

CAUTION : To restore an electrical connection with a heat-shrink sleeve, use only the tools and items in the approvec kit.

N.B. : Allow approximately 90 seconds for pre-heating of the hot air generator, one minute heating time depending o the cross-section of the wires and 3 minutes for cooling of the hot air generator.

![](images/8173542e31d48e0467384638ab5ac687cba000468bbad88f1f82ac38837702d8.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03TD

Method of operation (Applicable for a repair of 1 or more wires) :

Remove any covering from the wire (tape, sleeve, etc.) Cut and strip the end of each wire to be repaired ; Using the wire strippers

![](images/b217e71c2db7ae7c464a9691b99b4a550bef961dcf01554c3b013aad819f2ea2.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03UD

"A" Engage the stripped end of the 2 respective wires in the heat-shrink sleeve, twisting them.   
"B" Support the 2 wires and assemble them by heating the sleeve ; Using the hot air generator (seetable below). Sideways movement of the hot air generator may be necessary to obtain uniform heating of the heat-shrink sleeve.   
Put the contact in place in the connector.   
Visually analyse the condition of the contact.   
Insert the contact in its cell.   
Gently pull on the wire to check that the contact is locked.   
Restore the covering of the wire to guarantee protection at least identical to the existing protection.

![](images/72ca5b5b5165b14262c7cd845d096c1aad556364d4718423d0eefc8dc9b971de.webp)

![](images/c51607bc021ab19a587b65be80b3c9e171cd057f06b48b6c2bb749877750cef1.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03VD

N.B. : If the routing of the harness is modified, the harness must be clipped.

CAUTION : The tracks of a connector which are not connected electrically to the vehicle's harness must be fited wit a connection wire and have an end cap fited using the hot air generator.

CAUTION : If the repair requires the use of several heat-shrink sleeves, take care to stagger them to retain a minima volume.

5.10. Repair using additional wires (2 heat-shrink sleeves), wire unusable

![](images/cd70ebcdbd8934433b7ddfcb43972db3b0a4612aff30b72b3040b67f7db4de59.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03WD

The heat-shrink sleeves must be chosen according to the cross-section of the wire to be repaired :

Red sleeve : Wire between 0,35 mm2 and 1 mm2   
Blue sleeve : Wire between 1 mm2 and 3 mm2   
•Yellow sleeve : Wire between 3 mm2 and 5 mm2

N.B. : Crimp a heat-shrink sleve using the tools and items in the connection repair kit f the repair requires the use several heat-shrink sleeves, stagger them to retain a minimal volume.

Position the wires coming from one side in one sleeve and those coming from the other side in another sleeve taking care that the wires do not move away from each other. To make it easier to insert the wires in the heat-shrink sleeve, turn the heat-shrink sleeve slightly. Heat the sleeve using the hot air generator until the tin core melts and the surplus adhesive appears.

5.11. Method for applying a stitch weld sleeve

![](images/da014e4a7045ce9e7336f36c43911f426549d414f86ffe9b2035b136da18bc9e.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03XD

The heat-shrink sleeves must be chosen according to the cross-section of the wire to be repaired :

Red sleeve : Wire between 0,35 mm2 and 1 mm2   
Blue sleeve : Wire between 1 mm2 and 3 mm2   
•Yellow sleeve : Wire between 3 mm2 and 5 mm2

N.B. : Crimp the heat-shrink sleeve using the toos and items in the connection repair kit If the repair requires the us of several heat-shrink sleeves, stagger them to retain a minimal volume.

Position the wires coming from one side in one sleeve and those coming from the other side in another sleeve taking care that the wires do not move away from each other.

N.B. : Turn the heat-shrink sleeve slightly to insert the wires in the sleeve.

Heat the sleeve using the hot air generator until the tin core melts and the surplus adhesive appears. Approximately 90 seconds must be allowed for pre-heating of the gun, 1 minute for heating according to the crosssection of the wires and 3 minutes for cooling of the gun.

# 5.12. Method for restoring the covering

In order to restorethe harness covering, guarantee protection at least identical to the existing protection. If modifications are made to the routing, guarantee a minimum distance of 10 mm between the harness and its environment.

-or the taped harnesses, place the repaired part flush against the body of the harness and tape the whole using adhesive tape.

In the case of plastic sleeves, place the repaired part flush against the body of the harness then replace the sleeving

5.13. Method for selecting a protector

Mechanical protection : The mechanical protection is provided using a split spiral sleeve (E.g.: Engine compartment, Wheel arch). Thermal protection : The thermal protection is provided using a high temperature split spiral sleeve (E.g.: Near to the

exhaust in the engine compartment).

Joise protection : The noise protection is provided using a sound deadening sleeve during reworking requiring simple o nechanical protection (E.g. : Passenger compartment, Tailgate).

# 5.14. Restoring the covering

In the case of changes to the routing, a distance of 10 mm minimum must be guaranteed between the harness and its surroundings. A positioning device is compulsory to guarantee the positioning and orientation.   
Taped strands : Place the repaired part fush against the body of the harness and tape the whole using adhesive tape. Sleeved strands : Place the repaired part fush against the body of the harness then put the sleeving back in place. Closed sleeves : Avoid cutting the closed sleves in order to permit passage of the wire, otherwise place the repaired wire on top with appropriate covering.   
Open sleeves : It is compulsory to tape the openings after work.

5.15. Method for repairing the earth points

N.B. : In all cases, check the condition of the earth terminal contact/support/nut or bolt surface and clean it.

Several solutions are recommended.

ioldered square nut with broken self-tapping bolt or the thread of which is damaged :

If the bolt can be extracted, remove it, driland tap to M using a new M8 bolt then apply a tightening torque of 1 Nm ± 3 Nm   
If there is another earth nut nearby, extend the earth wire to reach this earth point, taking care to create a drip channel loop, Apply a tightening torque of 12 Nm ± 2 Nm

Stud which is badly soldered (TUCKER stud), broken or the thread of which is damaged :

If the stud soldering has failed, re-solder the old stud by brazing If the thread is damaged or the bolt is broken, solder a new stud by brazing

In the 2 cases of soldering, apply the method below :

Place a fire extinguisher near the work area   
Strip the location at which the pin is to be soldered   
Rotary sand the soldering location   
Solder the stud or the pin using the gun provided for this purpose   
Apply anticorrosion protection   
Put the removed components back in place

Soldered square nut with slackened self-tapping bolt :

If the M6X100 self-tapping boltis simply slack, retighten the bolt applying a tightening torque of 12 Nm ± 2 Nm Ifthe bolt has to be removed, fit a new 100 selftapping bolt, engage it manually in the existing thread take care not to create a new thread) then apply a tightening torque of 12 Nm ± 2 Nm

Earth on the gearbox slackened :If the bolt M8x125 is simply slack, retighten by applying a tightening torque of 17 Nm : 3 Nm.

# 6. Specificities : Hybrid vehicles

The harnesses of the 200 V network in hybrid vehicles can be repaired, with the exception of the shielded cable Replacement of the shielded cable is imperative if there is any damage to the cable or its connections.

ESSENTIAL : For the harnesses of the 200 V network, on hybrid vehicles (low voltage range of 50 V to 100, the personnel must have the authorisation according to the type of operation of the publication UTE C 18-550.

If the reworking is carred out by a third party, a contract must be drawn up for the work between the supplier and the company that it employs, before the work is carried out.

ESSENTIAL : All work relating to the connectors and contacts must be carried out by qualified and trained personnel.

The wirer wil take all measures necessary to avoid a change of personnel during the period of quality reworking in the reworking sector.

# 7. Failure detected / Circumstances of use

# 7.1. Wire broken

Apply the following methods in order :

. Method for checking a wire (5.1)   
, Method for stripping a wire (5.3)   
Method for selecting a wire (5.2) (In the case of an unusable wire)   
Method for restoring the covering (5.12)   
Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL :If the wire is unusable, cut the wire at the accessible points (near the connectors) and appy section 4.1 observing 2 rules : Remain in the same harness, retain the numbering of the wires (Cut the wire in such a way as to retain the numbered ends).

ESSENTIAL : In the case of a vehicle under warranty, if more than 4 wires are cut, the harness must be replaced.

# 7.2. Burnt wire

![](images/9c1a63e53ccdde88fff3bc94565509485317a08cca92f438dc3aaf562e5a2e31.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03YD

"d" Burnt wire. Apply the following methods in order : Method for stripping a wire (5.3)

JUMPER III - D6AM03P0 - Repair : Electrical harnesses

Method for selecting a wire (5.2) Method for restoring the covering (5.12) Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

N.B. : Re-cut more than 5 cm from the hot point and strip the wires; check that there is no sign of burning in the stripped part of the wire.

CAUTION : After analysing the fault, eliminate its cause ; Check allof the vehicle functions, the blown fuses.

CAUTION : In the case of a vehicle under warranty, the harness must be replaced.

CAUTION : In the case of a vehicle which is not under warranty, if more than 4 wires are burnt, the harness must be replaced.

# 7.3. Missing wires in the harness

Apply the following methods in order :

Method for selecting a wire (5.2) Method for selecting a contact (5.6) Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

# 7.4. Faulty splice

Apply the following methods in order :

, Method for stripping a wire (5.3) Method for selecting a wire (5.2) Method for applying a stitch weld sleeve (5.9) Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL : Cut the wire level with the splice.

7.5. Wire cut at the connector outlet / Contact unclipped or pulled out / Contact oxidised

![](images/4955443141c3a3e29dec40bd6f85f52957c3a69bec676317e9f4513aae359618.webp)  
Figure : D6AM03ZD

"e" Wire cut at the connector outlet.   
7.5.1 - Pre-wired connector available from the Replacement Parts Department (Contact + wire assembly). Apply the following methods in order :

Method for unclipping a contact (5.5) • Method for stripping a wire (5.3) • Method for selecting a wire (5.2) Method for selecting a contact (5.6) , Method for positioning a contact in its cell (5.7) Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL : f the contact is oxidised, replace the contact, create a low harness point at the connector outlet (modify the drip channel routing) and depending on the degree of oxidation, add grease in the connector (contact cleaner).

7.5.2 - Pre-wired connector available from the Replacement Parts Department. Apply the following methods in order :

Method for stripping a wire (5.3) Method for restoring the covering (5.12) •Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL :If the contact is oxidised, replace the contact, create a low harness point at the connector outlet (modif the drip channel routing) and depending on the degree of oxidation, add grease in the connector (contact cleaner).

No component of the connector available from the Replacement Parts Department.   
Replace the harness .

# 7.6. Wire cut at the overmoulded connector outlet

Apply the following methods in order : Method for checking a wire (5.1)

Method for stripping a wire (5.3) •Method for selecting a wire (5.2) (In the case of an unusable wire) Method for restoring the covering (5.12) •Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL :If the wire is unusable and a passage hole is available, fit a grommet ; If an additional wire is available use it and carry out the operations on each side of the overmoulded connector.

ESSENTIAL : If more than 4 wires are cut, the harness must be replaced.

# 7.7. Trapped wire

![](images/0ce28294ad47496f0d90d536d5211546575e9d42e4db0d217883b09b32964313.webp)  
Figure : D6AM040D

Trapped wire. Apply the following methods in order :

Method for checking a wire (5.1)   
, Method for stripping a wire (5.3) Method for selecting a wire (5.2) (In the case of an unusable wire)   
Method for restoring the covering (5.12)   
Method for selecting a protector (5.13)

ESSENTIAL :If the wire is unusable, cut the wire at the accessible points (near the connectors) and apply section 4.1 observing 2 rules : Remain in the same harness, retain the numbering of the wires (Cut the wire in such a way as to retain the numbered ends).

ESSENTIAL : If more than 4 wires are trapped, the harness must be replaced.

7.8. Stripped wire

Apply the method for selecting a protector (5.13).

7.9. Faulty crimping of a contact (Electrical resistance too high) Apply the method for tin soldering (5.4).

7.10. Faulty earth point Apply the method for repairing the earth points (5.14).

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

# 3. Special features

LUK clutch discs do not have damper hubs.   
The noise generated by the gearbox is fitered by the double damping flywheel (DVA) and not by the clutch disc hub. On the MLGU6 gearbox The LUK clutch mechanism includes an automatic wear adjustment device that requires a special tool for refitting.

(2) Compensation springs.

3. Preparation for removal

3.1. Checking - Cleaning

Visually check :

The flywheel face for damage or scores The flywheel for wear The condition of the starter ring gear , The clutch mechanism (2)

If there is oil in the clutch mechanism (2) :

Contröler I’'état de la bague d'’étanchéité du vilebrequin Contrler 'état de la bague d'étanchéité de l'arbre primaire

CAUTION : Ne pas réutiliser un disque d'embrayage dont le moyeu a des traces d'oxydation ou traces de graisse.

Désoxyder et dégraisser les pièces suivantes ; Using a degreaser Index "N1"  :

The clutch housing   
• The primary shaft   
• The clutch bearing guide (according to equipment)   
• The clutch fork (according to equipment)

N.B. : En cas de corrosion importante, utiliser une brosse métallique sans détériorer les pièces.

# 3.2. Greasing

CAUTION : Respecter rigoureusement ’'étape du graissage.

![](images/d5e6a596086b639dbf0ebfe537318f1096c0c8f946660543ec98a5d612d5dc7f.webp)  
Figure : B2BG08FD

CAUTION : Protect the interior of the clutch housing from splashes of grease.

Vehicles equipped with a gearbox that has a mechanical clutch bearing Spray a litte grease MOLYCOTE G-RAPID PLUS (aerosol) on the splines of the primary shaft and on the clutch bearing guide tube  (at "b" and ""). Vehicles equipped with a gearbox that has a hydraulic clutch bearing : Grease the splines of the primary shaft with MOLYCOTE G-RAPID PLUS  (at "").

CAUTION : Ne pas souiller la garniture du disque d'embrayage ; Risque de patinage.

Mettre en place le disque d'embrayage () sur larbre cannelé et effectuer plusieurs translations pour répartir la graisse.   
Déposer le disque d'embrayage .

![](images/b8b09b6adc004f1051c18eaa6b66e72d6eb8e1636305dc40f0bee7dc7f891ea3.webp)  
Figure : B2BG08GD

CAUTION : An excess of grease wil contaminate the clutch friction plate and cause noise in neutral, slipping o juddering of the clutch.

"d" : Traces de graisse présentes sur un disque d'embrayage pollué suite à un surplus de graisse.   
"e" : Traces de graisse présentes sur un carter d’embrayage pollué suite à un surplus de graisse.

| CAUTION : Nettoyer toute trace de graisse susceptible d'tre projetée sur la friction en rotation.

Remove the surplus grease on the top of the grooves and the end of the input shaft using a cloth.

N.B. : La pelicule de graisse déposée sur les éléments en rotation doit ètre la plus fine possible afin d'éviter le projections.

# 1. Preliminary operations

Remove the air filter and air inlet duct assembly.

CAUTION : Mark the level of brake fluid in the reservoir before carrying out the operation.

Remove the brake fluid reservoir cap .

1.1. Assembly with hydraulic clutch control slave cylinder

![](images/15380b1dc60646c7d11acffc237e331a8f09b618f42687f292e44ae06a757091.webp)  
Figure : B2BI00JD

CAUTION : The end of the transparent pipe must be submerged into the brake fluid.

Drain the hydraulic clutch control circuit :

Couple a transparent pipe onto the bleed valve (1)   
Plunge the end of the transparent pipe into a receptacle containing brake fluid, placed lower down than the hydraulic clutch control slave cylinder   
Press the locking clip (2)   
Pull the clp (3) by one notch in the direction of the arrow (open position)

1.2. Fitting with hydraulic stop

![](images/23e5831c6aaaba700573d1c4076c8f415d27b0ec8cc179445f75d662605a7521.webp)  
Figure : B2BG046D

Couple a transparent pipe onto the bleed valve (4).

CAUTION : The end of the transparent pipe must be submerged into the brake fluid.

Plunge the end of the transparent pipe into a receptacle containing brake fluid, placed lower down than the hydraulic clutch control circuit bleed.   
Open the bleed valve (4).   
Action the clutch pedal manually to drain the hydraulic clutch control circuit.   
Close the bleed valve (4).   
Uncouple the transparent pipe from the bleed valve (4).

The cover under the steering wheel The floor carpet

Figure : B2BG06ND

The clip (6) The supply pipe (10) of the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder (7)

N.B. : Plug the supply pipe (10) of the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder (7).

Remove the clip (8).   
Uncouple the hydraulic clutch control pipe (9).

N.B. : Plug the hydraulic clutch control master pipe (9).

Remove the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder (7) (turn a quarter turn anticlockwise).

2.1. Assembly with hydraulic clutch control slave cylinder

# 3. Refitting

Grease (according to assembly) :

The master cylinder rod ball joint With grease ESSO NORVA 275 The slave cylinder rod end piece  With grease MOLYKOTE BR2 PLUS

3.1. Assembly with hydraulic clutch control slave cylinder

Pass the pipe (13) into the support (15).   
Reclose the support (15).

Refit : The (14) bolt The pipe (13)

Close allof the clips retaining the pipe (13).

Refit :

The hydraulic clutch control slave cylinder (11) The 2 bolts (12)

Push back the clip (3).   
Pull on the locking clip (2).

3.2. Fitting with hydraulic stop

Refit : The pipe (16) The hydraulic stop (17) The bolts (18)

# 3.3. Subsequent operations

Refit the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder (7) (Rotate a quarter turn clockwise). Couple up :

The supply pipe (10) on the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder (7)   
The clip (6)   
The hydraulic clutch control pipe (9)

Refit the clip (8).

Connect the hydraulic clutch control master cylinder thrust rod to the clutch pedal. First assembly :

Refit the pin (5) Lock the pin (5) a quarter turn clockwise

Second assembly :

Refit the pin (5) Clip and reconnect the connector

Refit :

The cover under the steering wheel The floor carpet

# 4. Additional operations

Fill the brake fluid reservoir to its maximum capacity.   
Bleed the hydraulic clutch control circuit (see the relevant operation).   
Bring the brake fluid level to the level marked previously.   
Refit the fluid reservoir cap.   
Refit the air filter and air inlet duct assembly.

# BLEEDING : HYDRAULIC CLUTCH CONTROL

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations .

ESSENTIAL : During the bleed operations, take care to maintain the level of brake fluid in the reservoir by topping i up (if necessary). Use new brake fluid only.

CAUTION : Do not use automatic bleed equipment (risk of foaming of the brake fluid in the hydraulic circuit).

N.B. : For the bleed operation 2 operators are necessary.

Chock and lift the vehicle on a 2 column lift.

![](images/038cfa36fe2c0cb8a07b7060cafc61d2ba8506c7ba408af56a88106a0bc73b00.webp)  
Figure : B2BI00JD

Couple a transparent pipe onto the bleed valve (1).   
Sink the end of the transparent tube in a container containing brake fluid, located lower down than the clutch slave cylinder .

CAUTION : The end of the transparent pipe must be submerged into the brake fluid.

Press the locking clip (2).

Pull the clip (3) by one notch in the direction of the arrow (Position open).   
Action the clutch pedal manually through its entire travel rapidly 7 times.   
Leave the clutch pedal at the lower end of its travel during the last manoeuvre.   
Push back the clip (3) (closed position). Allow the clutch pedal to rise to the upper position.   
Fill the brake fluid reservoir to its maximum capacity.   
Press the locking clip (2).   
Pull the clip (3) by one notch in the direction of the arrow (Position open).   
Action the clutch pedal manually through its entire travel rapidly 7 times.   
Keep the clutch pedal at the lower end of its travel during the last manoeuvre.   
Push back the clip (3) (Closed position).   
Uncouple the transparent pipe.   
Top up the brake fluid level to the MAX. level in the brake fluid reservoir.   
Press the clutch pedal rapidly 40 times.   
Lower the vehicle.   
Start the engine.   
Apply the handbrake.   
Engage a gear. Check that clutch mechanism friction begins at a dimension "A" of 40 mm or more (the dimension (A) is given as a guide).   
Repeat the bleed operations (if necessary).

Figure : B2BP2PXD

Figure : B2CM05CD

The gearbox casing (2) The bolts (3) (one screw out of two) ; Tighten to 1,8 ± 0,1 daN.m

Fit : •The tools [14a], [14b], [14c] The dial gauge [15]

Rotate the primary shaft a few turns.   
Set the dial gauge to zero.   
Push the shaft axially, upwards,.

CAUTION : The play should be between 0,06 and 0,15 mm.

If the value read on the dial gauge is not correct, repeat the seting. Adjustment shims between 0,8 and 1,4 mm with a variation of 0,05 mm. Remove :

N.B. : Clean the primary shaft and the stop guide by hand using a metal brush in order to eliminate alltraces o oxidation.

ESSENTIAL : Clean the input shaft completely along its entire length, over its entire periphery and in the grooves.

Protect the interior of the clutch housing from splashes of grease.   
Spray the recommended lubricant evenly onto the thrust guide and the primary shaft.   
Grease the fingers of the clutch fork .

N.B. : For these operations, use the product MOLYKOTE SPRAY RAPIDE (Aerosol).

Remove the surplus grease on the top of the grooves and the end of the input shaft using a cloth.

CAUTION : An excess of grease wil contaminate the clutch friction plate and cause noise in neutral, slipping o juddering of the clutch.

ESSENTIAL : If the clutch disc is reused, the disc hub must be free of traces of oxidation.

On refitting, the clutch stop must be on its guide and positioned by the clutch release fork.

# 1. Check: air conditioning compressor

CAUTION : Before carrying out any work on the air conditioning compressor, top up the air conditioning circuit charge If the air conditioning circuit failure persists : Make the following checks.

# 1.1. Preliminary checks

Visually check : The air-conditioning compressor :

Check that the frame has not suffered any knocks and that it is not distorted   
Check that the pulley has not suffered any knocks or bangs   
Check that the clutch engages when the coil is supplied with 12V   
Check the condition of the supply cable and of the connector   
Check that the body of the air conditioning compressor is not cracked (at the air conditioning compressor fixing   
points)   
Check that the air conditioning compressor intake and discharge ports are not damaged

![](images/e871954c9c4116fb4b4babe4e95b8e3cbdb6bfdf7ae6e4493d5ac160f367c6ec.webp)

![](images/20b4bf8cc379f794c2017891ee68c07e3841b621f980cf0de22c2ae605ab2007.webp)

Interpretations of the pressures measured in the air conditioning circuit (Vehicle stationary, engine running)

![](images/ada363fc8e11e4e058ee8ef7fddcc76b3690e7c51f3694b75d824d616d591cfe.webp)

UMPER II - C5HB012VP0 - Technical note : Check of the air conditioning circui   
![](images/880470b691d77cc60e1114fb940a406e1f3d66eecfa8d0094041708b9b3133d1.webp)

# 1.2. Check with tool

Check the air conditioning compressor (The recommended tools should be used).

N.B. : See instructions for use : Tooling .

# 1.3. Oil level check

ESSENTIAL : The compressor lubricant is extremely hygroscopic, use new fluid for any operation.

There are 3 different cases :

Repairs to a system that has no leaks   
Slow leak   
Rapid leak

1.4. Work on the circuit (Without leak)

Use of filling and recycling equipment not fited with an oil trap :

Drain the low pressure fluid circuit as slowly as possible to prevent the compressor oil from being drawn out of th system   
The circuit is filled with refrigerant without the addition of oil

Use of filling and recycling equipment fitted with an oil trap :

Drain the refrigerant circuit conforming to the instructions in the equipment's manual   
Measure the quantity of oil recovered   
Add the same quantity of oil as that recovered

# 1.5. Slow leak

Slight leaks do not cause losses of oil, apply the procedure described for repairs to a system without leaks.

# 1.6. Rapid leak

This type of incident can produce a loss of oil, as well as cause the circuit to breathe.

Perform the following operations :

Replace the filtering and drying cartridge (If necessary) Evacuate the maximum amount of oil possible (when replacing the faulty component) Before or during the R134.a refrigerant refilling process, introduce 80 cc of new oil into the system

# 2. Air conditioning system check

Fit the tool in its place(Tools recommended in the Service documentation ). Perform the following operations :

Close all the air vents Start the engine Open the front left vent Select the central and side air vents on the air conditioning control panel Position the air circulation control on "entry of exterior air" Set the A/C system to the maximum ventilation setting Reduce the temperature as much as possible   
− Operate the air conditioning for 5 minutes

# 3. Interpretation of the values (reminder)

N.B. : Values relating to use of the diagnostic tool.

# 3.1. Undercooling (SR)

The under-cooling represents the difference between the condensation temperature and the refrigerant temperature a he air conditioning condenser outlet.

The under-cooling indicates the quantity of refrigerant (in liquid state) in the air conditioning circuit.

![](images/38cf1c1111e3947bb1250b67e38136a30bf6abec56d1ac1aa42dcfab204799c8.webp)

UMPER II - C5HB012VPO - Technical note : Check of the air conditioning circui

![](images/8afc5f11b76aa82d36ee9033f18666b39425c5fd20c1636b5a69dab738593567.webp)

# 3.2. Over-heating

The over-heating represents the diference between the refrigerant temperature at the evaporator outlet and the evaporation temperature.

The over-heating indicates the quantity of refrigerant (in gaseous state) in the air conditioning circuit.

![](images/6902e4032d9ad3e0cfe53cbfde2ef7c68e104460c3181e57c734556e8d3011da.webp)

# 3.3. Temperature of the blown air "u"

The temperature of the blown air should be between 2°C and 10°C.

# REPAIR : IMPACT ON THE LAMINATED WINDOWS PRINCIPLES OF REPAIR

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations  .

1. Tooling   
1 Repair kit (Manual injection ).   
1 Repair kit (Injection using the pressure/vacuum pump ).

N.B. : Refer to the tools catalogue.

# 2. Windscreen repair area

CAUTION : Read the repair manual in full.

![](images/ed551216a9f560d4b9bf3cedd7c232f34e7ec331cbffbcb128e998f0f6f281d8.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06WD

"A" = 300 mm.

ESSENTIAL : The repair of a windscreen in the field of vision of the driver, see "A", is prohibited.

ESSENTIAL : If the impact is more than 50 mm : Replace the windscreen.

# 3. Types of impact

# 3.1. Bubble or half-bubble impacts

![](images/7568a2318dc819626f3d03184af81f5d40c9585a83c15820b0998db51a24ebc0.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06XD

"B" = 20 mm (Max ).

N.B. : Formation of a small hole at the point of impact and a core in the form of a cone is created.

3.2. Star impact

![](images/64c3a83d76b6d2fb930b9483b0fb07bbfbf76674921166083235a6b129f422cd.webp)  
Figure : C5CM06YD

"C" = 50 mm (Max ).   
Formation of cracks or worse, spreading from the point of impact.

3.3. Star bubble or combination impact

![](images/701d7b215c2ed2adf83d065065e6ba852fbdc78c54cdb59180f3376fe6e1470a.webp)  
Figure : C5CM08PD

"D" = 50 mm (Max ).   
Formation of cracks or worse, spreading from the point of impact.

# 4. Precautions regarding use

N.B. : Numerous factors can affect the result of a repair.

The most important points to be complied with are the following :

Check for the presence of moisture in the impact Check that the temperature of the window is between 10°C and 30°C Protect the resin from ultraviolet rays   
• Control the amount of pressure during the injection of the impact

# 4.1. Humidity

N.B. : If moisture is present, dry out the impact using the heating lamp.

CAUTION : Heat the laminated window moderately using the heating lamp as any other excessively strong anc excessively violent heat source may enlarge the impact and crack the laminated window.

# 4.2. Temperature

The ideal temperature for repairing a laminated window is between 10°C and 30°C.

4.3. Ultraviolet rays Repair away from ultraviolet rays.

4.4. Pressure

Follow the pressure level recommendations in the repair manual.

5. Repair

N.B. : Proceed in the same way for an athermic windscreen.

Place a protective cloth on the bonnet for setting down the tools.   
Clean the laminated window around the impact using a dry, lint-free cloth.

N.B. : Do not spray any products onto the impact.

5.1. Fitting

![](images/52ccf25ebf1767ba637e65d0143981b0ce32ce71bbe8c4dcfcf8a8aa8d4f4536.webp)  
Figure : C5CM070D   
Figure : C5CM08QD

Exert slight pressure on the impact at"a" using your thumb to ensure that itis free of the beginnings of any cracks

а х е

Apply adhesion product to the suction cup.   
Put the rear view mirror in place inside the passenger compartment level with the impact.

UMPER I - C5CM0103P0 - Repair : Impact on the laminated windows Principles of rep

# N.B. : The mirror will serve as a guide throughout the repair.

![](images/f4e223323cb5968ace71038307cd255342d55c084602220a183a30656bf236dc.webp)  
Figure : C5CM08YD

Dril out the point of impact until contact is made with the sheet of polyvinyl butyral ; Using a drill and bit.

# 5.2. Injection process

2 Processes for injecting the resin :

1 Manual process   
1 Process using a pressure/vacuum pump

N.B. : Refer to the repair manual : Before removing the injection equipment, check that there are no more particles air in the impact.

# 5.3. Drying and finishing

Apply a drop of finishing resin.

Figure : C5CM08ZD   
Figure : C5CM090D

Put a small plastic sheet on the finishing resin.   
Allow the small plastic sheet to rest naturally so that the finishing resin covers the whole impact.

MPER II - C5CM0103P0 - Repair : Impact on the Iaminated windows Principles of rep

N.B. : Do not touch the finishing resin with your fingers.

![](images/b2d5afb57e3212d0c0d8dd996fb080f6c3a2e34b1db062b8af18690bead81b53.webp)  
Figure : C5CM091D

Put the ultraviolet lamp in place on the smal plastic sheet on the exterior side of the laminated window.   
Leave to dry for 15 minutes (minimum).

Remove :

The ultraviolet lamp The plastic sheet

![](images/9953d8268a6fcde811bc11ca249a56c989c483e6415162a48779d35e52f6e240.webp)  
Figure : C5CM092D

Scrape of the surplus finishing resin using the scraper.

CAUTION : Scrape offthe surplus perpendicular to the laminated window and not parall (risk of removing the entire layer of polymerised resin).

# 1. Tooling

Glass scratch repair kit.

N.B. : Refer to the tools catalogue (Bodywork Family).

# 2. Windscreen repair area

CAUTION : Read the repair manual in full.

![](images/42ebb9e1fa0d7b6aafa701632fd46a1605769d1adf127b028762a909f18c42ad.webp)  
Figure : C5CM095D

"A" Zone of driver's field of vision in which any repair is forbidden (220 mm).

N.B. : Any repair in the driver's field of vision may constitute a hindrance of vision.

# 3. Precautions regarding use

N.B. : Always store the discs in individual plastic bags to avoid contamination. Excessive heat may break the glass.

JUMPER II - C5CM0106P0 - Repair : Scratch on glass

ESSENTIAL : Keep the temperature of the glass under control to prevent i from breaking.

Mixing 5 litres of distilled water with the dose provided permits several repairs of optimum quality. If the polisher bounces on the glass during the operation, increase the level of water and the angle of the polisher slightly.

ESSENTIAL : Use the polisher with extreme care (Splashes of water).

# 4. Scratch

CAUTION : A scratch which can be detected with a fingernail is considered deep and therefore irreparable.

Repairable scratches : Slight scratches Very slight scratches

ESSENTIAL : Follow the repair process using the discs is descending order, blue, orange and white.

# 5. Preparation

![](images/09459297ca070144fc1aae6ca9997f99fc3a51c3ab5c1f69bed96add7f56ce6b.webp)  
Figure : C5CM096D

Examine the scratch (at "a") to be repaired and determine its repair.

N.B. : To see the surface to be worked on more easily, mark the interior of the window using a black marker.

Clean the glass.

Protect the vehicle against slashes of water.

# ESSENTIAL : Use distilled water.

Fill the water reservoir with the full dose provided for 5 litres of water.   
Pump the coolant reservoir several times to pressurise it.   
The pipe must be connected to the polisher.   
Check that the red water flow valve is in the closed position.

![](images/377a4106ee7139d2da7f644635bc718ddaf4370983530c745b8e2f9c1d711088.webp)  
Figure : C5CM097D

# 5.1. Polishing

CAUTION : Too litle water may result in an increase in the temperature of the polishing disc and shorten its service life; too much water slows down the polishing process.

'urn the valve anticlockwise until a few drops of water begin to flow from the centre of the polishing head

ESSENTIAL : Follow the repair process using the discs is descending order, blue, orange and white.

Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be polished.   
Eliminate the scratch (at "a") ; Using the polisher.   
Polish the area (at "b").   
Clean the glass ; Using a scraper.   
Visually check the progress of the repair.   
After a few minutes of polishing, the scratch begins to disappear.   
Continue polishing until the scratch has disappeared completely.

# 5.2. Final polishing

There are 2 options for the final polishing stage.

1 option :

Use the white disc ; Using the polisher   
Increase the flow and quantity of water   
Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be repaired   
Polish the area (at "b")   
If the polisher begins to bounce, increase the flow of water   
Continue the final polish, until a satisfactory result is achieved

2 option :

Use the foam disc ; Using the polisher Apply the polishing fluid or powder to the foam disc Add a few drops of water to the foam Hold the polisher flat and keep it above the surface to be repaired Polish the area (at "b") Continue the final polish, until a satisfactory result is achieved • If cloudy marks remain after polishing, Use option 1 to achieve a satisfactory result

# 4. Re-assembling

ESSENTIAL : Always replace the damaged fixings.

Carry out the re-trim operations in the reverse order to the stripping operations. Tighten :

The nuts (5) to 2 ± 0,4 daN.m The bolts (17) to 2 ± 0,4 daN.m   
The bolts (4), (8), (10), (13), (16), (25), (37), (52) to 4,2 ± 0,8 daN.m The bolts (64), (66) to 5,3 ± 0,7 daN.m   
The nuts (14) to 4,3 ± 0,8 daN.m

Check all the equipment works.

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

# REPLACE : PRE-TENSIONING PARTS (FOLLOWING TRIGGERING OF THE AIR BAGS AND SEAT BELTS) - INSTRUCTION FOR REPLACEMENT OF FAULTY PARTS AND REPAIRABILITY OF THE HARNESS

Replace (In the event of impacts and following each triggering) :

Gas generator connectors (If damaged) •Control unit The elements listed below

# 1. Parts required

Regardless of the activation of the pyrotechnic equipment (impact or accidental triggering), the triggering unit of this equipment (or air bag ECU) must be changed.

ESSENTIAL : The special gas generator connectors must be replaced if they are damaged.

# 1.1. Triggering with impact

![](images/0a1690d34b96226ee8ed5193c01d7a33514d99e2c977801f8d0210a99a27ddff.webp)

N.B. : In the case of a vehiclfitted with 2 satellites (front and rear), change the 2 satelites even if one of the module was not triggered.

# 1.2. Accidental triggering without impact

![](images/3311767d87d16d631111c4440669de5d1e6fddb2dbdf0022522dc38a0db16eb3.webp)

JUMPER wlae Pei part Fllg ig eir baandl ti relt f r

![](images/470ed9aa6a76745d246de590ed9396512d49dcff45dc44f6feabbdc3a1d89d69.webp)

2. Visual methods for checking whether a component has been deployed

The triggering of an inertia reel is indicated by :

Air bag warning light illuminated on the instrument panel A fault code recorded and read using the diagnostic equipment A characteristic noise of balls noticed following removal of the inertia reel

# 3. Instructions for replacement of parts

The parts replaced will be deployed in the following cases :

Parts to be destroyed Parts which have passed their validity date

CAUTION : Therefore, all warranty return parts required will be returned without being deployed.

# 4. Conditions for transporting explosive components

The packaging recovered from the replacement part must be used to transport the parts.

5. Repairability of the harness

The repair of all of the harnesses is permitted using strictly RAYCHEM welded unions observing the operating procedure.   
Compulsory method of repair : Equipment (RAYCHEM).

ESSENTIAL : Repair of the wires must be carried out with heat shrink sleeves and outer covers (-).1228 kit).

Replace the generator connecting harness if the connector is damaged following triggering.   
In the case of a module supplied with a harness, the whole will be replaced.

# 6. Check after operation

ESSENTIAL : After any work performed on the central airbags system, cary out a fault reading with the diagnostic equipment .

# 1. Deactivation

![](images/05212d2aaafd62c8b056fe8fb4b85b705a1ca2857da5c06a3398656730d6e1ec.webp)  
Figure : D1AP03CD

Disconnect the battery negative cable (1).   
Protect the cable and the negative terminal in order to prevent any contact.

CAUTION : Wait for at least 5 minutes before performing any operations (discharging of the airbag ECU powe reserve).

CAUTION : The ECU must not be removed with the connector still connected under any circumstances.

Disconnect the airbag ECU connector.

# 2. Activation

ESSENTIAL : The area of the airbags and pyrotechnic seat belts should be kept clear, both of objects and of people

Ignition off : Connect the airbag ECU connector.   
Connect the battery negative cable.   
On the driver's side, door open, ignition on, keeping the steering wheel module activation area clear.   
Check the system is operating correctly by checking the airbag fault LEDs.

N.B. : After disconnecting the battery, some electronic systems (injection, safety auto-reverse system . ) need ar

# 1. Drain and refill

Unscrew the power steering reservoir cap .   
Raise the vehicle and support on axle stands, wheels free. Uncouple the low pressure pipe union (1).   
Turn the steering in both directions, from lock to lock.   
Recover the power steering fluid.   
Plug the low pressure pipe union (1).

![](images/ae9abb0d207fad4bbf969b0931fd1bfd008f0d5914e7141217e9f198b3ebde8c.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7NUD

N.B. : Do not re-use the power steering fluid.

# 2. Refilling

Use fresh power steering fluid.   
Oil quality : TUTELLA GI/E. "A" : Power steering fluid level when cold (20 °C).   
"B" : Power steering fluid level when warm (90 °C).   
Fill the power steering fluid reservoir to the maximum level.

![](images/3676688cc0c5141255fd0d11013c6edbdaa18e2990e52dc2efe8fa309c93ff76.webp)  
Figure : B3EP19CD

# 3. Bleeding

N.B. : Return the vehicle to its wheels.

Engine stopped :

Fill the power steering fluid reservoir to the maximum level (If necessary) Turn the steering in both directions, from lock to lock (3 times minimum) •Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level (If necessary)

engine running :

Wait one minute Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level (If necessary) Move the steering from lock to lock, until there is no point of resistance

Stop the engine.   
Top up the power steering fluid to the maximum level.   
Check there are no leaks.

# JUSTMENT : PLACING AT THE REAR AXLE TIGHTENING REFERENCE HEIGHT

CAUTION : The suspension components of the rear axle must be tightened with the vehicle at the reference height Failure to observe these conditions would result in the distortion of the silent blocks or an ineficient tightening of the suspension blade clamps.

# 1. Vehicle with metal suspension

![](images/75a6c9a3dbdacc2b93057fae39a7c9dc0587438d667908dc203305d89728349a.webp)

Figure : B3BP1G9D   
![](images/e0bd65d766d111f74f209490c287975beb2ec674fda92f541b5d639ea772e2d5.webp)

The height " A"is measured between the suspension blade front fixing centreline and the underneath ofthe rear axle crossmember.   
The reference height is obtained by loading the vehicle.

2. Vehicle with pneumatic suspension

![](images/61e8418ecf40947c009e5114a2ac23a180279235f2bb1c8d3cb8c3027b8663e0.webp)

Figure : B3BF007D   
![](images/5339cacf0b7f604a2c5fff82180a520e4992b718815fffea78b5130e3b0f39a2.webp)

"B" : Measure between the measurement zone "b" underneath the mounting for the pneumatic suspension units and the measurement zone "a" under the rear axle crossmember.

# 2. Removing

Disconnect the battery negative terminal.   
Untighten the wheel screws (left hand front).   
Lift and support the front of the vehicle.   
Remove the left-hand front wheel. Remove the nut (1) (left side).   
Uncouple the steering balljoint (2) ; Using tool [1].

![](images/be4c5da4a4ce5e8104d03468c16b2b204bbe2f16c0fe7625bf062a6c05945bc2.webp)  
Figure : B3FP7JJD

Figure : B3BP1CDD

Remove the 3 bolts (4).

Move the hub carrier forward. Remove (on each side) :

Remove the nuts (3), (5) • The washer (6) The silentblock (7) The connecting rod (8)

![](images/d0955c9b53015547ac35d8f2fe7626ae56f41ee97dfc14d15bf10b10bae4f59c.webp)  
Figure : B3CPOBDD

Remove the bolts (9) (on each side).

![](images/e9bd15b1ca550ca441dc4133f9c75ad81060ab9b995eca84328f3e48d31d899c.webp)  
Figure : B3BP1CED

Attach the steering rod to the hub carrier .   
Remove the front anti-roll bar (10) from the left-hand side with a downward rotation (following the arrow ).

# 3. Refitting

# N.B. : Always fit new Nylstop nuts.

Refit (on each side) :

The front anti-roll bar (10)   
The bolts (9) ; Tighten to 5 ± 1,3 daN.m   
The connecting rod (8)   
The silentblock (7)   
The washer (6)   
The nuts (5), (3)   
Position the hub carrier lower ball joint.   
Refit the bolts (4) ; Tighten to 11,5 ± 0,4 daN.m.   
Couple up the steering ball-joint (2).   
Refit the nut (1) ; Tighten to 8 ± 0,7 daN.m.   
Fit the wheel.   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten (on each side) : The nut (3) to 5,6 ± 0,5 daN.m The nut (5) to 5,6 ± 0,5 daN.m

# 2. Removing

Untighten the wheel screws (front).   
Lift and support the vehicle with front wheels suspended.   
Remove the front wheels. Remove bolts (2).   
Disengage the wheel speed sensor (1).   
Suspend the wheel speed sensor (1).   
Remove the brake pads (see the relevant operation). Remove the fastener (3) and disengage the flexible union .   
Liberate the wiring harness (at "a"). Remove bolts (4).   
Disengage the brake caliper (5).   
Leave the caliper hanging (5).   
Unlock the transmission nut .

# 3. Refitting

Position the tool [4]]in the front pivot opening .   
Turn a quarter turn to open the pivot.   
Engage the front pivot (16) on the suspension leg .   
Refit bolt (13).   
Remove the tool [4].   
Tighten the bolt (13) to 12 ± 0,4 daN.m.   
Position the ball-joint housing (12).   
Refit the bolts (11).   
Tighten the bolts (11) to 11,5 ± 0,4 daN.m.

Refit :

The silentblock (15) The washer (14) • The nut (9)

Couple up the steering balljoint (8).   
Refit the nut (7).   
Tighten the nut (7) to 8 ± 0,7 daN.m.   
Refit the driveshaft nut (6).   
Immobilise the hub from rotation using tool [1].   
Tighten the driveshaft nut : 47,5 ± 4,75 daNm.   
Remove the tool [1]. Lock each drive shaft nut with the help of tool [3].   
The flat part "b" of the tool should always face outwards.

![](images/32adc05ab449de1d05a836841d17f527134855dfa4b383b5c3e53801eed18fae.webp)  
Figure : B2FP06MD

CAUTION : The nut collar must be locked in the opposite direction to tightening.

Refit :

The brake caliper (5) The new bolt (4) (Pre-coated with a thread-locking product)

Tighten the bolt (4) to 3,4 ± 0,2 daN.m. Reposition :

The harness (at "a") • The brake hose The clip (3)

Fit the brake pads (see the relevant operation).   
Refit the wheel speed sensor (1) (see the relevant operation).   
Tighten the bolt (2) to 0,8 ± 0,3 daN.m.   
Reposition the harness of the wheel speed sensor .   
Fit the wheels.   
Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten the nuts (9) and (10) to 5,6 ± 0,5 m.daN.   
Tighten the wheel bolts  .

![](images/3d1a0f76cd421dc6a3489f7cc1fd3de17025c24bae8ed6f11d3c6a4f8bc40166.webp)  
Figure : B2FG039D

ESSENTIAL : The nut collar must be locked in the opposite direction to tightening.

Remove the tool [6310-T].

Refit :

The front wheels • The front wheel bolts The right-hand protector under the engine The protective panel under the engine

Return the vehicle to its wheels.   
Tighten the front wheel bolts  .   
Fill gearbox with oil and ensure correct level (see the relevant operation).

CAUTION : Perform the operations to be carried out following reconnection of the battery.

# 7. Additional operation

Refit the drive shafts.

# 1. recommendations

CAUTION : The use of impact wrenches to refit the wheel bolts and wheel anti-theft bolts is strictly prohibited.

CAUTION : The wheels are always tightened with dry bolts.

CAUTION : When installing a new steel wheel for the first time, Always double tighten the wheel, to avoid any risk o slackening.

N.B. : Double tightening consists of tightening to the specified torque followed by slackening then retightening to the specified torque.

Ensure that the anti-theft wrench is positioned correctly on refitting.

CAUTION : Tighten the wheel bolts using a torque wrench.

# 2. Tightening torques : road wheels

![](images/ee856340f55b6a7c8340f0e3cab3abbce90657cc65e905f2aa272c06f135d29b.webp)

# 3. Wheel valve

3.1. Vehicles not equipped with tyre under-inflation detection system Always replace the wheel valves when changing the tyres.

CAUTION : Vehicles DS3 Racing ; Tighten the wheel valves to 0,4 daNm.

3.2. Vehicles fitted with a tyre under-inflation detection system Observe the tightening torque of the wheel valve nuts : Tighten to 0,8 daN.m.

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

# 1. Removing

Remove the sensor trim .

![](images/df78b13301484cfe025553778c050641618c44c0898f8a623b3977f94b41e941.webp)  
Figure : C5DP06VD

Disconnect the connector "a".   
Unclip the spring ( 2).   
Extract the rain sensor ( 1) from its base by hand (perpendicular to the windscreen).

# 2.Refitting

ESSENTIAL : Fit a new rain sensor.

N.B. : The cleanliness of the rain sensor and of the windscreen are essential for the correct operation of the system.

Clean the windscreen and the inside of the base of alldirt, bonding residue and other particles; using a non-fluffy pap towel and glass detergent.

CAUTION : Chemical detergents are not authorised.

Remove the protection cover.

CAUTION : Do not touch the contact surface with the skin or with any object.

Place the rain sensor ( 1) in its base.   
Lock the spring ( 2).   
Connect the connector "a".

# 3. Checks

Insert the key in the vehicle ignition.   
Start the engine.   
Activate the automatic windscreen wipe (position I or "AUTO").   
A single wipe of the front windscreen confirms that the automatic mode has been activated.   
Spray water onto the rain sensor zone.   
Check the functioning of the automatic windscreen wipe.   
Place the wiper switch in position 0.   
Stop the engine.

PEUGEOT

![](images/7b5dc98f48b9268857f8a59ae06e66bbf38d1a035bd02a7b27ee3846bfb14f69.webp)

# PEUGEOT BOXER WORKSHOP MANUAL 2006 - 2017

You will see that this workshop manual is for the Citron Jumper. Don't worry, the Peugeot Boxer was badged the Citroën Jumper in a lot of countries and is also known as the Citroen Relay, Fiat Ducato, Peugeot Manager and the Ram Promaster. Your workshop manual deals with the 3rd generation Peugeot Boxer which was launched in 2006. All the models (Jumper, Ducato, Relay, Boxer, Manager etc) allshare the same design and engineering, with only subtle trim changes between each brand. So don't worry, you have the correct manual.

# 1. Foreword

# 1.1. Units of pressure

1/ Units of pressure in bars.

N.B. : One bar has the advantage of being close to the average atmospheric pressure at sea level.

2/ Unit of pressure in millimetres of mercury (symbol: mmHg) or Torr (symbol: Torr).   
This unit of measurement of pressure was origially defined as the pressure exerted at 0°C by a 1 milimetre column of mercury, later indexed to the atmospheric pressure.   
The pressure values indicated in the tables below are the values read on the pressure gauge (Relative pressure).

N.B. : Relative pressure is equal to absolute pressure minus atmospheric pressure.

# 1.2. Units of tension

The SEEM unit measures by deflection of the static tension of the belt, by deforming a portion of its length.

# 2. Removing

# 2.1. Common operations

CAUTION : Replace the torsional vibration damper double pulley for a distance travelled greater than or equal t 160000 km, when the accessories drive belt is replaced.

Place the vehicle on a 2-post lift.   
Disconnect the battery negative terminal.

Remove :

The protection plates under the engine The front right wheel

CAUTION : Prior to removal, and before any subsequent refittig of the ancillary drive belt that has been removed, it is compulsory for the engine to be at ambient temperature (Below 0 C). In alother cases, replace the ancillay drive belt.

N.B. : Removing it with the engine hot causes irreversible and invisible damage to the ancillary drive belt.

CAUTION : If replacing it, cut and remove the ancillary drive belt.

CAUTION : Check that the tool [0198-P] is correctly positioned between two teeth of the flywheel; or turn the crankshaft to correctly position the tool.

Move aside and secure : The starter motor  .

![](images/8adf2ae6deda2c0eff39186a9cd75823cca084e05073710fc77e6b53e631c09a.webp)  
Figure : B1BG2YHD

Position the tools [0198-P], [0198-E].   
Secure the assembly using the starter motor bolts. Remove the accessories drive pulley fixing bolts (1).   
Slacken the fixing bolt (2) of the ancillary drive pulley by 2 cm.

![](images/c85cb12e732bce9f59ab4b0efa1f001ca1aee2f1b011307be7d2b3144f36c952.webp)  
Figure : B1BPSHAD

![](images/0d108019c10936de98c9ee89a08b63a5a3503dea4c58e0a5cef52b017d52d321.webp)  
Figure : B1BPSHBD

Move aside the ancillary drive pulley, pivoting it on the fixing bolt (2).

CAUTION : Mark the direction of fitting of the accessories drive belts if they are to be reused.

Remove the accessory drive belts.

2.2. Vehicle with air conditioning

![](images/c280b2b537295a948a1499fe4ede92247a8d9d619f3d503eb841ef0e24615ab1.webp)  
Figure : B1BPSHCD

Compress the dynamic roller tensioner (3) ( as "a") (anti clockwise) ; Using tool [1608-E].   
Peg ( as "b") ; Using tool [0188-Q1].   
Remove the accessories drive pulley fixing bolts (1).   
Slacken the fixing bolt (2) of the ancillary drive pulley by 2 cm.

![](images/a51dec372d1f88b78e155b2376affc93cf1ccb97354c160a62312c3e553ca1cb.webp)  
Figure : B1BPSHDD

Move aside the ancillary drive pulley, pivoting it on the fixing bolt (2). Disconnect the air conditioning compressor connector (4); By means of a screwdriver. Remove :

The dynamic roller tensioner (3) fixing bolts (5) The dynamic roller tensioner (3)

CAUTION : Check that the rollers (6),(7) and (8) rotate freely (no play and no stiffness).

Remove the accessory drive belts.

CAUTION : Adhere to the tightening torques

CAUTION : Replace the torsional vibration damper double pully for a distance travelled greater than or equal t 160000 km, when the accessories drive belt is replaced.

CAUTION : Make sure that the ancillary drive belts (9) and (10) are corectly positioned in the grooves of the various ancillary drive pulleys.

Refit :

The accessories drive belt (9) with the dynamic roller tensioner (3)   
The dynamic roller tensioner (3) fixing bolts (5) The accessories drive belt (10) Turn the power steering pump pulley ; Using a spanner ( as "c") (In the direction of the arrow ).   
Guide the accessories drive pulley by hand.   
Maintain the effort ( as "c") (In the direction of the arrow ).

3.1. Cleaning to be carried out just before refitting

# 3.2. Checking the flatness

Check the flatness of the cylinder head : Maximum permissible bow = 0,1 mm.

3.3. Checking the protrusion of the pistons

CAUTION : Remove the crankshaft immobilisation and locking tool.

![](images/ae3355e816e430b7caad19e0911a0788cf8de3fdb77834920799fb57d1544cff.webp)  
Figure : B1DG0RAD

CAUTION : The sealing surfaces must be perfectly clean : No signs of impact, no traces of scaling permited.

Place the pistons of cylinders 1 and 4 at top dead centre ; Using the dial gauge. Note down the stand-proud of the pistons in relation to the cylinder block seal face. Pistons 1 - 4 :

Place the dial gauge in a stable position on the cylinder block gasket face ; Set the dial gauge to zero Move the dial gauge over the 2 checking points "a", "" (Piston) (10 mm from the edge) ; Read the values Calculate the average of the 2 values measured

JUMPER IlB1DG0160P0 - Removing - Reftting : Cylinder head (on vehicle)

Pistons 2 - 3 : Repeat the operation.

# 3. Filling the cooling system

CAUTION : If the cooling system is contaminated, rinse with clean water.

CAUTION : Always use new coolant.

CAUTION : Each filling operation must always be followed by a cooling system degas operation.

JUMPER IlB1Gl0138P0 - Drain and refill - Reilling - Bleeding : Cooling system

Close the bleed screw when the fluid is flowing freely without any air bubbles.

3.2. Filling using the tool for filling the cooling system by vacuum

CAUTION : Always use new coolant.

Connect the hose (1) (at "a") ; Using tool [0165-2].

# N.B. : Refit new clips .

Close the bleed screw .   
Put the equipment for filling by vacuum [01102] in place on the expansion bottle .

CAUTION : To avoid entry of air into the circuit, provide for 20 % additional coolant.

Prepare a receptacle of coolant containing the quantity of fluid drained + 20 %.

N.B. : The receptacle must be positioned slightly lower than the equipment for filing by vacuum.

Wait 10 seconds and check that the value obtained does not drop Fillthe cooling circuit completely and wait for the return to 0 bar (diagram "D")

N.B. : The quantity of coolant filled should correspond to the quantity of fluid drained.

Repeat the operation until the cooling system is full(if necessary).

JUMPER Il - B1Gl0138P0 - Drain and refill - Reilling - Bleeding : Cooling system

CAUTION : Remove the equipment for filing by vacuum [01102] and rinse the assembly with clean water.

4. Degassing and checking the cooling system

Fit the charging cylinder, closer and adaptor assembly on the expansion botle, in the case of draining using the tool for filling by vacuum [01102].   
Open the rod on the filling cylinder .   
Start the engine.

N.B. : The air conditioning control should not operate during this phase.

4.1. Toutes motorisations sauf norme de dépollution EURO 6 Keep the engine speed at 15002000 rpm, up to the second cooling cycle (cooling fan(s) cuting in and out).

CAUTION : Check that there are no coolant leaks.

# 4.2. Diesel engine Euro 6

The cutting in of the fan assembly for 10 seconds indicates the switch to after sales degas mode.   
Accelerate to an engine speed above 2300 rpm for more than 10 seconds to switch to degas mode.   
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 rpm until the fan assembly cuts in again.

4.3. Degassing and checking the cooling system (continued)

CAUTION : Check that the level of coolant in the filling cylinder is sufficient.

Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Do not remove the filling cylinder while the engine is hot.

Leave the engine to cool.   
Blank the filling cylinder using the blocking rod .   
Remove the filling cylinder , plug and adapter assembly.   
Check the coolant level when cold.   
Top up the coolant to the "max" level (Cold).

CAUTION : Do not fill the system past the max mark.

Refit and tighten the cap on the header tank .

CAUTION : Check that the cooling system fillr cap is locked (For bayonet cap).

3. Preliminary checks

3.1. Low pressure fuel circuit

Check the following components :

The quantity of fuel in the tank : 15 litres minimum   
Fuel qualityif in doubt over the fuel quality, use an auxiliary tank with a filter, filled with fuel which you know where it came from)   
•That there are no leaks on the high pressure fuel circuit

# 3.2. Electrical circuit

Remove the engine style cover . Check the elements which could cause system malfunctions :

The battery charge The deactivation of the engine immobiliser •The condition of the connectors and electrical harnesses

JUMPER IIB1HD0151PO - Check : Fuel high pressure supply circuit

The classfication of the injectors ; Using the diagnostic equipment

4. Checking the fuel high pressure circuit

4.1. Check : Fuel pressure regulation

![](images/a1b73ef18457e3dcd089908ba5be494d0733f99fc73d72b9d7773a85510f52c1.webp)  
Figure : B1HDZL2D

Disconnect injectors (at "a").

Connect the diagnostic tool to the vehicle's diagnostic socket ; Select in succession the following menus :

, Parameter Measurements menu • Fuel circuit information • Fuel pressure ordered - Measured fuel pressure

Operate the starter for 5 seconds ; Read the maximum values of the ordered and measured pressures on the diagnosti tool simultaneously.

CAUTION : The ordered and measured pressures must be identical (± 40 bars) and 120 bars minimum.

N.B. : If the pressures read are identical, the system is providing suficient pressure to start and operate normally Confirm the preliminary checks, otherwise contact the technical assistance platform.

N.B. :If the pressures read are different, the system does not have the pressure required : Check the leak return fron the pump and from the injectors.

Connect the connectors (at "a").

CAUTION : Close the union ; Using tool [1617-J].

Abide by the following conditions :

Fuel pressure regulator disconnected (at "c") Unions on the low pressure fuel return pipe plugged

Operate the starter motor for 15 seconds.

CAUTION : The maximum volume collected should not exceed 25 ml.

N.B. : In the case of a volume which exceeds this value, replace the high pressure pump then repeat the check.

CAUTION : Carefully clean, plug and store the tool used.

Remove the tool [1613-G].   
Disconnect the fuel pressure regulator (at "c").   
Connect the union (at "b").

# FORCED REGENERATION : PARTICLE FILTER (TECHNICAL NOTE)

ESSENTIAL : Observe the safety and cleanliness recommendations.

ESSENTIAL : Wait at least one hour before carrying out any work on the exhaust line.

# 1. Tooling

Diagnostic tool.

# 2. Forced regeneration of the particle emission filter

ESSENTIAL : Respect the safety and cleanliness recommendations that are specificto high pressure diesel injection (HDi) engines.

ESSENTIAL : Where the recommended installation is not available, carry out the forced regeneration of the particle filtr outside the workshop, on an area of hard standing and remote from any inflammable materials. Make the work area secure. Ensure that no one passes or stands behind the vehicle during the forced regeneration. Put the vehicle in the "high" position (vehicle with hydraulic suspension). Check that there are no aerosols or inflammable products inside the boot. Wear heat-resistant gloves. Connect the vehicle to an approved gas extractor for this type of operation.

CAUTION : Check that the level of fuel in the tank is sufficient (minimum 20 litres).

CAUTION : Check the following fluid levels : Engine oil ; Coolant.

CAUTION : Check : The tightness of the turbocharging hoses (Risk of uncoupling).

ESSENTIAL : Remove the under-engine protection.

Start the engine and allow it to warm up (65°C minimum).   
Connect the diagnostic tool on the vehicle's central socket.

Carry out :

Fault reading (Engine ECU) Fault clearing

Trigger the particle emission filter forced regeneration cycle ; Using the diagnostic equipment.   
After the regeneration cycle : Alow the engine to run at idle, with the bonnet open, to help the cooling.   
Stop the engine.

ESSENTIAL : Wait at least one hour before carrying out any work on the exhaust line. Wear heat-resistant gloves.

Refit the under-engine protection .

New vehicles delivered to customers now have a hydrometer which permits direct displaying of the charge status.

# 1. Application

This procedure applies to all ready-to-use batteries.   
They are fitted on new vehicles or sold as Replacement Parts (boutique, warehouse, gondola end.….).   
The batteries must guarantee quality and reliability which meet the requirements of our customers.   
They are an addition to the new vehicle preparation ranges distributed for each model of the range.

# 2. Recommended tools

Approved charging equipment : See garage equipment catalogue or, failing this, obtain a limited voltage charger Approved battery cable.

# 3. General principles for charging batteries

:omply with the maximum voltage indications and the nominal current level in relation to the type and size of the batter

Never apply an excessive voltage or current   
Use a charger suited to the battery and the type of charge required   
Do not use a rapid charger or, if the charger has this function, use the normal charge function   
Check the condition of the battery

N.B. : The effectiveness of the charge depends on the condition of the battery.

# 4. Precautions to be taken

Do not charge :

A faulty battery (White hydrometer)   
A battery coated with sulphate (Depositing of a superficial layer of lead sulphate on the plates)   
A warm battery (Risk of thermal racing and damage)

5. Charging procedure

5.1. Preliminary operations

![](images/8df7c30c3b55b3cfd878e9c8be564d254c4be63a452b3b308a16fd0f033566fe.webp)  
Figure : D1CP03JD

Remove the battery (1) located underneath the passenger compartment floor.

CAUTION : If the hydrometer is white, the battery is faulty : Replace the battery.

Check the conformity of the battery :

Sealing of the case   
Absence of electrolyte leaks Absence of apparent signs of impact or cracks   
, Status of the hydrometer

N.B. : Date of manufacture (If the battery was manufactured more than 6 months ago : Replace the battery).

# 5.2. Charging

Follow the operating instructions given by the manufacturer of the charger .

Check the clamps and terminals are clean .If the terminals are covered with sulphate (whitish or greenish deposit), str and clean them.

The recharging operation must be carried out in a ventilated environment away from naked flames or any sources of sparks to prevent any risk of explosion and fire.

Do not recharge a frozen battry;i must first be thawed out to prevent the risk of an explosion;if it has frozen, have the battery checked before recharging by a specialist; they willcheck that the internal components have not been damagec and that the casing is not cracked, which would mean that toxic and corrosive acid could leak.

case of batteries with topping of up of the electrolyte only :

Connect the battery to the charger starting with the positive cable Check the level  15 mm above the plates) and top up with distilled water (if necessary)

CAUTION : In the case of batteries which do not require maintenance, removal of the caps and topping up with fluid is strictly prohibited.

# 5.3. Automatic charger

Use the normal charging programme (Rapid charging prohibited).

5.4. Charger with limited voltage

Adjust the charging current to 1/20 of the capacity(example: 45Ah provides a charging current of 2,25A) for a charging time of 6 to 12 hours.

# 5.5. Limited voltage charger

Charge with a voltage limited to 14,8 V for 12 hours with a current limited to 1/4 of the capacity.

5.6. Precautions to be taken (Battery charge)

Monitor the progressof the charge regularly, ensuring in particular that the battery does not get excessively warm or does not start to bubble. When the charge is complete, first switch off the charger and then disconnect the battery.

# 6. Check following charging

Check the colour of the hydrometer :

If it is green : The battery is correct   
Refit the battery on the vehicle   
fit is not green: An additional charge is necessary, until the hydrometer turns green, without exceeding the time defined   
After 2 unsuccessful charging cycles, the battery is faulty   
Replace the battery
